confirmed.title: Toggling Alert zone in edit mode wipes the 'Recently above' history even when the edit is cancelled (Back) or toggled back
confirmed.trigger: Settings > Alert zone > OK (edit) > Right (or Left) once, then Back to undo; or press Right twice so the zone ends where it started; then press Done.
confirmed.impact: Observed: `store.remove(HISTORY_KEY)` runs on every arrow press, before the edit is committed; cancelEdit() restores settings.alertZone but not the history, and the restartFeed scheduled 700-900 ms later re-reads the now-empty key (live.mjs:276), so the Radar layout's 'Recently above' list and Synthwave's last-seen line go blank for a change the user undid. Expected: Back puts everything back as it was when OK was pressed; a no-net-change edit loses nothing.
confirmed.evidence: app.mjs:324 `else if(el.id==='set-zone'){settings.alertZone=...;store.remove(HISTORY_KEY);return zoneChanged();}` and cancelEdit() at app.mjs:383-392 only does `Object.assign(settings,before)`; live.mjs:276 `let history=store.get(HISTORY_KEY)||[]` on every feed start.
confirmed.fix: Do not clear the history inside adjustSetting. Snapshot it alongside editSnap in select() (`editHist=store.get(HISTORY_KEY)`), and clear it only in stopEdit()/the commit path when `before.alertZone!==settings.alertZone`; restore it in cancelEdit(). Alternatively record the zone kind the history was built with and drop it lazily in restartFeed when the kind actually differs.
reasons: UPHELD: Confirmed from code. #set-zone carries data-edit (web/index.html:54), so OK enters edit mode via select() (web/app.mjs:509), which snapshots settings only. Each arrow press in editKey (app.mjs:375) calls adjustSetting, and app.mjs:324 executes store.remove(HISTORY_KEY) synchronously before any commit. cancelEdit() (app.mjs:383-392) restores only settings via Object.assign and schedules restartFeed in 700 ms; restartFeed (app.mjs:163-167) stops the old feed, discarding its in-memory history, and the new startLive seeds history from store.get(HISTORY_KEY)||[] (web/live.mjs:276), now empty. radar.mjs:51 renders this as 'Recently above'. Pressing Right twice (net no change) removes the key twice with no restore. The list only survives by race if the old feed polls with planes inside the zone during the 700-900 ms window and re-writes the key (live.mjs:320). Suggested fix in the claim (snapshot history alongside editSnap, clear only on commit when alertZone actually changed, restore in cancelEdit) is sound. Severity lowered to P3: the loss is limited to a self-healing display list that refills as aircraft pass, and the clear on a genuine zone change is intentional; only the cancelled/no-net-change edit path is defective.

UPHELD: Confirmed from the code. web/app.mjs:324 runs `store.remove(HISTORY_KEY)` synchronously on every Left/Right press on the Alert zone row while editing, before any commit. select() at app.mjs:509 snapshots only `settings` (`editSnap=rest`), and cancelEdit() at app.mjs:383-392 only does `Object.assign(settings,before)` and schedules restartFeed 700 ms later; nothing re-saves the history. The zone is a binary toggle, so two presses return to the original value yet both presses have already wiped the key. restartFeed (app.mjs:163-167) calls start() which in live.mjs:276 does `let history=store.get(HISTORY_KEY)||[]`, so the new feed begins with an empty list; core.mjs:112-113 builds model.recent from `states[IDS.candidate].attributes.history`, which radar.mjs:190 ('Recently above') and synthwave.mjs:154 ('s-last') render. The only thing that could incidentally repopulate storage is the still-running old feed persisting its in-memory history at live.mjs:320, and that happens only if a poll with a plane inside the zone lands within the ~700-900 ms before restart, which is not a reliable guard. No other try/catch, caller, or default restores the list. The claim's trigger, impact and fix are accurate; severity stays P2 since it is a cosmetic data loss of a derived list that refills over time, not a crash or persistent-settings corruption.

UPHELD: Confirmed by code. #set-zone has data-edit (assets/index.html:54), so OK enters edit mode and select() (web/app.mjs:509) snapshots only settings into editSnap. Every arrow press in edit runs adjustSetting, which at web/app.mjs:324 toggles settings.alertZone and unconditionally calls store.remove(HISTORY_KEY) before any commit. cancelEdit() (app.mjs:383-392) restores settings via Object.assign(settings,before) but never restores the history key, and both zoneChanged() (900 ms) and cancelEdit() (700 ms) schedule restartFeed, which stops the old feed (discarding its in-memory history) and calls start(), where live.mjs:276 reads history=store.get(HISTORY_KEY)||[] — now empty. The same loss happens with Right pressed twice (zone ends where it started) followed by OK/Done. The emptied list drives model.recent via core.mjs recentSightings, which the Radar (radar.mjs:190) and Atlas 'Recently above' panels and Synthwave's last-seen line (synthwave.mjs:154) display, so a user who backs out of the edit or toggles back loses up to 20 saved overflights and sees a blank panel until new planes pass. Reproducible, user-visible, non-crashing data loss from an undone action: P2 stands.

confirmed.title: Back while editing a Settings value can also close Settings: the 350 ms Back de-duplication is skipped on the editing path
confirmed.trigger: Settings > any row with data-edit (e.g. Alert radius) > OK > Right > Back, on a device where the hardware Back press is reported both by App.tsx (injectJavaScript __whatsupBack) and as a page keydown (Escape/keyCode 4) - the exact situation the dedupe comment describes.
confirmed.impact: back() returns from `if(editing)return cancelEdit();` before `lastBack` is updated. The second report of the same press then sees editing===null, passes the `now-lastBack<350` check and runs close(), so one Back press both undoes the edit and closes Settings (or, if the second report arrives first, the order is cancel then close just the same). Expected: Back while editing only undoes the edit and stays on Settings.
confirmed.evidence: app.mjs:532-537 `function back(){ if(editing)return cancelEdit(); const now=Date.now();if(now-lastBack<350)return;lastBack=now; // the app and the page may both report one press ...close(); }`
confirmed.fix: Run the de-duplication first: `const now=Date.now();if(now-lastBack<350)return;lastBack=now; if(editing)return cancelEdit(); if(adj)return endAdjust(); close();` (or set lastBack inside the editing branch).
reasons: UPHELD: The code path is real. web/app.mjs:604 routes every page keydown for Escape/GoBack/BrowserBack/Back/keyCode 4 to back() BEFORE the `if(editing)return editKey(e)` dispatch at :623, so editKey's own cancelEdit branch (:378) is dead for those keys; and src/App.tsx:163-172 injects window.__whatsupBack() (= back()) on hardwareBackPress whenever overlayRef is set (Settings open → syncApp at app.mjs:264 reports overlay:true). So if one physical press is delivered both ways, both deliveries hit back(). In back() (app.mjs:532-537) the editing branch returns at :533 without touching lastBack, so the second delivery sees editing===null (cleared by stopEdit inside cancelEdit), passes `now-lastBack<350` (lastBack is 0 or stale), sets lastBack, and falls through to close(), popping Settings. Order of the two deliveries does not matter: both call back(), the first cancels the edit, the second closes. Also confirmed: cancelEdit ends with the restore+busy() path and the editing row is already un-marked, so there is no second guard that would stop close(). The only thing not verifiable from the repo is the precondition itself: no file (TESTING.md, QA-REPORT.md, PRESHIP-REPORT.md, App.tsx comments) records that Vega actually delivers one Back press both as hardwareBackPress and as a page keydown; the dedupe at :534 (present since the initial commit e5df0be) was written as a "may" defence, and the editing path was added later in 4f73c0a without honouring it. If the device never double-delivers, there is no user-visible effect. Severity lowered to P3: conditional on an unconfirmed device behaviour, the outcome is a reverted edit plus an unexpected Settings close (recoverable with one Play/Pause press, no data loss), and the fix is a one-line reorder (dedupe before the editing branch, or set lastBack inside it). Worth fixing before ship since it is trivially safe.

UPHELD: Code confirms the claimed ordering. web/app.mjs:532-537: back() returns via cancelEdit() when `editing` is set, before `lastBack` is updated. Both Back delivery paths funnel into back(): the page keydown handler (app.mjs:604, Escape/GoBack/keyCode 4 → back(), checked before the `if(editing)return editKey(e)` dispatch at :623, so editKey's own Escape branch at :378 is never reached) and the host (src/App.tsx:163-172, BackHandler → injectJavaScript('window.__whatsupBack()') whenever overlayRef is true, which it is while Settings is open per syncApp at app.mjs:264). cancelEdit() (app.mjs:383-392) only resets editing/editSnap and restores settings; nothing in it, in close(), or in the keydown handler sets lastBack or otherwise suppresses a second report. So if one hardware press is reported by both paths, the first call cancels the edit and the second passes the 350 ms check (lastBack is still from an older press) and runs close(), closing Settings. No guard elsewhere covers this. What cannot be verified from the repo is whether Vega actually delivers the press twice: the only evidence is the author's own comment ("the app and the page may both report one press"), there is no test for it (tests/ has nothing on lastBack/keyCode 4), and TESTING.md device rows (e.g. line 36 rapid mashing, line 107 window-bearing edit) never exercise Back while editing. Suggested fix stands: move the `now-lastBack<350` check and `lastBack=now` above `if(editing)return cancelEdit();`.

Both reporters do reach back(): App.tsx:163-171 injects `window.__whatsupBack()` on hardwareBackPress whenever overlayRef is true (Settings is an overlay via syncApp, app.mjs:264), and the page keydown handler at app.mjs:604 routes Escape/keyCode 4 to back() BEFORE the `if(editing)return editKey(e)` branch (editKey's own cancelEdit at :378 is dead for Back). confirmed.title: Location search started on a previous visit can paste its results into a freshly opened, empty Location screen
confirmed.trigger: Settings > Location, type 3+ letters on the on-screen keyboard (the 900 ms debounce starts runSearch), press Back before the geocoder answers (slow network; the race allows up to 25 s), then OK on Location again (or choose a place and reopen Location later).
confirmed.impact: openLocate() resets entry/results but does not bump searchSeq, and close() does not either; when the old request resolves the guard at line 483 passes (`seq===searchSeq`, `layer.id==='locate'`), so the results box fills with matches for text that is no longer in the entry field and lastQuery is set to the stale query. The user sees places unrelated to the (empty) entry; 'Try again' re-runs the stale query. Expected: a search that was abandoned by leaving the screen never shows up.
confirmed.evidence: app.mjs:483 `if(seq!==searchSeq||layer?.id!=='locate'&&!layers.some(l=>l.id==='locate'))return;` vs app.mjs:501-505 `function openLocate(help){entry='';setText('entry-text','');$('results').replaceChildren();...open('locate');}` (no searchSeq++), and close()/closeAll() at 251-262 never touch searchSeq.
confirmed.fix: In openLocate() add `searchSeq++;clearTimeout(searchTimer);lastQuery='';` (and do the same when close()/closeAll() hides the locate layer), or compare the result's `q` against the current `entry.trim()` before showing it.
reasons: UPHELD: Confirmed from web/app.mjs: searchSeq is only declared (:441), incremented inside runSearch (:464) and checked at :483; openLocate (:501-505) resets entry/results but never bumps searchSeq or clears searchTimer, and close()/closeAll() (:251-262) do not touch it. A runSearch started on a prior visit therefore survives Back; if the Location screen is reopened before the 25 s race settles, the :483 guard passes (seq===searchSeq, layer.id==='locate'), lastQuery is set to the stale query and show() paints its results into the empty-entry results box; 'Try again' (:526) re-runs that stale query. The window is narrow (result must land while locate is open again and before any key is typed, since typing bumps searchSeq) and the impact is bounded (stale but valid places are shown; choosing one still passes through the Confirm screen, so no wrong location is silently saved), so P3 rather than P2. Suggested fix (searchSeq++, clearTimeout(searchTimer), lastQuery='' in openLocate, or compare q with entry.trim() before show) is correct.

UPHELD: Confirmed from ~/overhead-tv/whatsup/web/app.mjs. runSearch (line 462-499) captures `seq=++searchSeq` and after awaiting up to SEARCH_LIMIT_MS=25000 only checks `seq!==searchSeq || (no locate layer open/stacked)` at line 483. Nothing invalidates an in-flight search when the Location screen is left: close() (251-261) and closeAll() (262) never touch searchSeq, searchTimer or entry, and openLocate() (501-505) only resets entry/entry-text/results without `searchSeq++` or `clearTimeout(searchTimer)`. So: with settings.place set (otherwise close() refuses to leave locate), type 3+ letters, Back before the geocoder answers, OK on Location again -> openLocate shows an empty entry; when the old promise settles, seq still equals searchSeq and layer.id==='locate', so line 484 sets lastQuery to the stale q and show() fills #results with matches (or the 'Try again' retry button) for text no longer in the field. Even a not-yet-fired 900 ms debounce timer survives close(): it fires with the old entry while the screen is hidden and starts the same stranded request. No other guard (typeKey, select, back, confirmPlace) covers this path. It is real but low-impact: requires a slow geocoder response plus a quick Back/reopen, the stale rows are still valid selectable places, and typing any key or pressing Search starts a new seq that supersedes it. Fix as suggested: in openLocate() (and when close()/closeAll() hide the locate layer) do `searchSeq++; clearTimeout(searchTimer); lastQuery='';`, or additionally require `q===entry.trim()` at line 483.

UPHELD: Confirmed by reading web/app.mjs. runSearch (line 464) captures seq=++searchSeq and, after the await, only checks `seq!==searchSeq || (layer not locate and no locate in the stack)` at line 483. close() (251-262) and closeAll() (263) never touch searchSeq or searchTimer, and openLocate() (501-505) resets entry/results but does not bump searchSeq. So: with settings.place set, type 3+ letters, debounce fires runSearch, press Back (close() pops to settings; an in-flight request that resolves now is correctly dropped by the layer check), then press OK on Location again while the request is still in flight: openLocate clears the entry, open('locate') makes layer.id==='locate', and when the request resolves the guard passes, lastQuery is set to the old query and the results box is filled with matches for text that is no longer shown. The suggested fix (searchSeq++ and clearTimeout in openLocate, or comparing q to entry.trim()) is correct. Severity is overstated though: the window is the geocoder round-trip (normally 1-3 s; 25 s only on a pathological network), the user must leave and re-enter Location inside it, and the consequence is a transient list of valid places under an empty entry that any keypress replaces with a fresh search (the 'Try again' path additionally pastes lastQuery back into the entry, so that case is self-consistent). No crash, no wrong location saved without the user explicitly confirming it on the Confirm screen. Realistic TV-user impact is a brief confusing display; P3.

confirmed.title: Cancelling Adjust position reached from the confirm screen throws away the search result and strands a first-run user on the dashboard
confirmed.trigger: First launch: Welcome > Change > type a ZIP > Search > pick a result > 'Adjust position' > press Back (cancel). Same from Settings > Location > result > Adjust position > Back.
confirmed.impact: startAdjust() calls closeAll() (closing confirm, locate and welcome) and endAdjust() does not reopen anything, so Back from the fine-tune map lands on the dashboard with the OLD (IP-guessed) location, the found place is discarded, and on first run `confirmed` stays false while the welcome card is gone (it returns on the next launch). The user must start the whole search over from Settings. Expected: Back from Adjust returns to the screen it was opened from (the 'Use this location?' card, or Settings).
confirmed.evidence: app.mjs:554-557 `async function startAdjust(place){ if(!place)return; closeAll(); adj={...}` and app.mjs:590-598 `function endAdjust(save=false){ const a=adj;adj=null;...; if(save){...choosePlace(...)}; if(lastModel)draw(lastModel);syncApp(); }` - no reopen on the cancel path.
confirmed.fix: Keep the layer stack while adjusting (hide overlays with the existing `.adjusting` stage class instead of closeAll()) and on cancel just remove the class and restore focus; or remember the origin (`adj.from='confirm'|'settings'`) and on cancel call `confirmPlace(pending)` / `showSettings();open('settings')` respectively.
reasons: UPHELD: Confirmed from the code. web/app.mjs:556 `startAdjust()` unconditionally calls `closeAll()` (app.mjs:262), which pops every layer (confirm, locate, settings, welcome) and sets focus to null. The cancel path is real: `back()` at app.mjs:535 does `if(adj)return endAdjust();`, and `endAdjust(save=false)` (app.mjs:590-598) only clears `adj`, removes the `.adjusting` stage class, redraws the dashboard and calls `syncApp()`; it never re-opens a layer or calls `confirmPlace(pending)`/`showSettings()`. Both entry points reach it: `case 'confirm-adjust':return startAdjust(pending)` (app.mjs:519) from the 'Use this location?' card, and `case 'set-adjust':return startAdjust(settings.place)` (app.mjs:517) from Settings. On the confirm path `pending` is never consumed on cancel, so the geocoded result is discarded and the user is on the dashboard with the previously applied place (on first run, the IP-guessed one from boot(), app.mjs:688, saved with confirmed:false). `confirmed` is only set true in `choosePlace()` (app.mjs:214) or 'welcome-ok' (app.mjs:513), neither of which runs on cancel, so the welcome card reappears next launch (app.mjs:674). Nothing in tests covers this (tests/test-whatsup.mjs only checks element presence). One nuance: the welcome card already auto-closes after 60 s with confirmed still false (app.mjs:693), so 'confirmed stays false' is partly by design; the concrete defect is that Back from Adjust drops the user to the dashboard instead of the originating screen and throws away the search result, forcing the whole Settings > Location > search flow again. That is a genuine UX/state bug in the first-run funnel but not data loss or a crash, so P2 is appropriate. Suggested fix stands: record the origin in `adj` (or avoid closeAll() and rely on the `.adjusting` class, which assets/whatsup.css:81-83 already uses to hide the layout) and on cancel reopen the confirm card via `confirmPlace(pending)` or `showSettings();open('settings')`.

UPHELD: Confirmed by reading the code; nothing elsewhere handles the cancel path. web/app.mjs:554-557 `startAdjust()` unconditionally calls `closeAll()` (line 262), which pops and hides every stacked layer (welcome -> locate -> confirm, or settings -> locate -> confirm) and leaves `layer=null`. The cancel path is `back()` (line 535) -> `endAdjust()` with save=false (lines 590-598), which only clears `adj`, removes the `.adjusting` class, redraws the dashboard and calls `syncApp()`; it never calls `open(...)`, `confirmPlace(pending)` or `showSettings()`. So Back from the fine-tune map lands on the dashboard with the previous `settings.place` (the IP guess on first run), `pending` is kept only as a dead variable with no UI path back to it, and on first run `settings.confirmed` remains false (only `welcome-ok` at line 513 or `choosePlace` at line 214 set it) while the welcome card is gone until the next boot (line 674). Both entry points exist in the UI: `#confirm-adjust` (web/index.html:101 -> select() line 519) and `#set-adjust` (web/index.html:53 -> line 517). No test covers this transition (tests only check the overlay ids exist). The only recovery is OK/Play-Pause -> Settings -> Location and retyping the query on the on-screen keyboard. Severity P2 is reasonable: no data corruption and the user can recover, but an explicit search result the user already picked is silently discarded by a single Back press, which is a real first-run flow defect on a TV where re-entry is expensive. The suggested fix (keep the layer stack and only toggle `.adjusting`, or record `adj.from` and reopen confirm/settings on cancel) is sound; note the `.adjusting` CSS at web/whatsup.css:81-83 already hides the layout, so hiding overlays via that class instead of `closeAll()` is a small change.

UPHELD: Confirmed in code. web/app.mjs:556 `startAdjust()` calls `closeAll()` (app.mjs:262), which pops every layer (confirm, locate, settings, welcome) and clears focus. The cancel path `back()` -> `endAdjust()` (app.mjs:535, 590-598) only clears `adj`, removes the `.adjusting` stage class, redraws the dashboard and calls `syncApp()`; nothing reopens the previous layer and `pending` is left unused. `choosePlace` is only invoked on the save path (`endAdjust(true)`), so the searched place is never persisted on cancel: `settings.place` remains the IP guess and, on first run, `settings.confirmed` remains false (it is only set by `welcome-ok` at app.mjs:514 or by `choosePlace`). The adjust panel itself labels the key as "<kbd>Back</kbd> cancel" (web/index.html:112), which a TV user reads as "cancel the nudge", not "discard the location I just found". Repro is exactly as claimed for both entry points (`confirm-adjust` at app.mjs:519 and `set-adjust` at app.mjs:517; the Settings path also silently closes Settings). Impact is a stranded dashboard with the wrong location and an overlay=false state so the next Back exits the app; recovery requires Play/Pause -> Settings -> Location -> retype and re-search. It is recoverable and causes no persistent data loss (welcome returns next launch), so P2 (not P1) is the right level; the suggested fix (keep the layer stack and only toggle `.adjusting`, or record the origin and reopen it) is cheap and correct.

confirmed.title: Up/Down on the Map radius row (edit mode) runs opposite to Up/Down on the dashboard
confirmed.trigger: Dashboard: press Up (map radius shrinks, 'closest' direction). Settings > Map radius > OK > press Up (map radius grows).
confirmed.impact: editKey maps ArrowUp to +1 (`Math.sign(10)`) so Up = wider in edit mode, while the dashboard handler maps Up to stepMap(-1) = closer. The same physical key zooms in on one screen and out on the other; users stepping the radius from Settings get the opposite of what the dashboard taught them.
confirmed.evidence: app.mjs:376 `if(dir)return adjustSetting(editing,editing.dataset.big!==undefined?dir:Math.sign(dir));` with dir={ArrowDown:-10,ArrowUp:10}; app.mjs:619 `if(dir==='up'||dir==='down'){e.preventDefault();return stepMap(dir==='up'?-1:1);}`
confirmed.fix: In editKey special-case set-map: `if(dir&&editing.id==='set-map')return stepMap(k==='ArrowUp'?-1:k==='ArrowDown'?1:Math.sign(dir));` or make the dashboard use the same sign.
reasons: UPHELD: Code path is real and reproduces by inspection. web/index.html:64 gives #set-map `data-edit`, so OK on the row hits app.mjs:509 (`editing=el`), after which arrow keys route to editKey (app.mjs:622 -> 372). editKey maps ArrowUp to dir=10; set-map has no data-big, so app.mjs:376 passes Math.sign(10)=+1 to adjustSetting, which at app.mjs:321 calls stepMap(+1) -> next larger MAP_RADII entry (wider). On the dashboard (no layer), app.mjs:619 maps ArrowUp to stepMap(-1) -> next smaller radius (closer). Same key, same setting, opposite direction. Edit-mode Left/Right (-1/+1) agree with the dashboard's zoom semantics only by accident of axis; Up/Down do not. Impact is a UX inconsistency with no data loss or crash (Back in edit mode restores the snapshot via cancelEdit, and the toast names the new value), so P3 is the right severity. The suggested fix (special-case set-map in editKey, or flip the dashboard sign) is sound; note the dashboard convention "Up = zoom in" is also what the comment at app.mjs:618 documents, so flipping editKey for set-map is the less disruptive choice.

UPHELD: Verified in code. web/app.mjs:373-376: editKey maps ArrowUp to dir=10, and since #set-map has no data-big, it calls adjustSetting(editing, Math.sign(10)=+1); app.mjs:321 routes set-map to stepMap(+1), which steps to the next larger MAP_RADII entry (wider). web/app.mjs:619: the dashboard handler calls stepMap(dir==='up'?-1:1), so ArrowUp = stepMap(-1) = closer. assets/index.html:64 confirms #set-map carries data-edit, so OK on the row does enter edit mode (app.mjs:509) and Up/Down then go through editKey. There is no special case for set-map in editKey or adjustSetting that flips the sign, so the same physical key zooms in on the dashboard and out in Settings edit mode. Left/Right in edit mode (Right = wider) are consistent with Up in edit mode, so the inconsistency is only Up/Down between the two screens. It is a real but low-impact UX inconsistency, not a functional failure: the value is clamped, the toast names the direction, and the user can simply press the other key. Severity P3 stands.

UPHELD: Code confirms the claim exactly. web/app.mjs:373-376: editKey maps ArrowUp to dir=10 and, because #set-map (web/index.html:64) has no data-big, passes Math.sign(10)=+1 to adjustSetting -> stepMap(+1) (app.mjs:321, 398-399), which moves to the next larger MAP_RADII entry (web/place.mjs:54). web/app.mjs:619: on the dashboard ArrowUp calls stepMap(-1), the next smaller radius. So Up really does widen the map in Settings>Map radius edit mode and narrow it on the dashboard; nothing in callers (select at app.mjs:509 sets editing for any data-edit row, keydown at 622 routes to editKey) prevents it. Impact for a TV user is small though: the row value and a toast ("Map radius N mi") update immediately on every press, the wrong direction costs one extra press, and Left/Right are the advertised edit keys ("OK to change", comment at 370). Note the edit-mode convention (Up = increase) is shared with Alert radius and the bearing rows in the same panel, so the suggested special-case for set-map would create an inconsistency between adjacent Settings rows; if changed, the dashboard mapping (or a shared helper used by both) is the better place. P3 is appropriate.

confirmed.title: Location screen opened from Settings before the first IP lookup finishes: Back is dead although Settings is beneath, and a second #locate is pushed onto the stack
confirmed.trigger: Clean install, during 'Finding your location…' (up to the 6 s IP timeout, longer on a flaky network): press Play/Pause (opens Settings, Location 'Not set'), OK on Location, then Back.
confirmed.impact: close() returns because `layer.id==='locate'&&!settings.place`, and syncApp() reports overlay=true (layers.length===1) so the app swallows the hardware Back too: no way back to the visible Settings screen until a place is chosen. confirmed.title: Tile count per map build is unbounded by latitude: 100-500 tiles at Alaska/Nordic homes, up to 4,200 (most with impossible x/y) at the 85° validator limit
confirmed.trigger: Set home (search or IP) to any high-latitude city and build a map. Measured with a fake network counting getBytes calls (tilecount.mjs in scratchpad, importing web/mapgen.mjs unmodified): Chicago 15 mi = 9 base + 50 detail tiles; Anchorage 15 mi = 25 + 114; Reykjavik 15 mi = 30 + 130; Tromsø 15 mi = 36 + 213, 50 mi = 162 base; Longyearbyen 15 mi = 100 + 538; lat 85° (accepted by place.mjs:42) 15 mi = 484 + 2,788 tiles of which 220 + 1,044 have y<0 or x>=2^z; 85° / 250 mi = 792 + 4,200 (3,570 impossible).
confirmed.impact: eachTile (mapgen.mjs:86-93) derives x0..x1 from dLon=lim/(69.172*cos) and y0..y1 from Mercator tileY, so the count grows ~1/cos²(lat); zoomFor() and DETAIL_SPECS pick zoom from radius only, and the comment at :17-20 ('2-9 at any radius') is only true near 40°. Tiles are fetched strictly sequentially with a 10 s timeout each; a Fairbanks/Anchorage user at 15 mi waits for 100+ z11/z12 tile downloads on every detail build (and again on every launch if the result exceeds the localStorage quota, see the quota finding), a Tromsø user for 200+. Impossible coordinates (negative y, x beyond 2^z) are still requested and each failed request costs two round trips (direct fetch then the native bridge, live.mjs:44-55). Rapid radius stepping (stepMap -> applyPlace 700 ms later) does not abort superseded builds, so several of these streams can run concurrently. There is no cap of any kind on tiles per build.
confirmed.evidence: mapgen.mjs:89-93: `const dLat=lim/69,dLon=lim/(69.172*cos); const x0=Math.floor(tileX(home.longitude-dLon,zoom)),x1=...; const y0=Math.floor(tileY(home.latitude+dLat,zoom)),y1=...; for(let tx=x0;tx<=x1;tx++)for(let ty=y0;ty<=y1;ty++){ const bytes=await net.getBytes(...)`  Measured: `Tromso r= 15 base z10: 36 tiles  detail z11: 213 tiles`, `Longyearbyen r= 15 base z10: 100 tiles  detail z11: 538 tiles`, `lat85 r=250 base z6: 792 tiles (600 out-of-range) detail z7: 4200 tiles (3570 out-of-range)`.
confirmed.fix: In eachTile clamp ty to [0,2^z) and wrap tx modulo 2^z (skip rather than request impossible tiles); lower the chosen zoom by round(log2(1/cos(lat))) (or pick zoom so that the x-range*y-range stays under a budget, e.g. 36 tiles), and add a hard cap that throws 'too many tiles' instead of looping. Consider aborting a superseded build (check a token inside the tile loop) when placeToken/detailToken moves on.

Every supporting assertion checks out in the code: (1) eachTile (mapgen.mjs:86-93) derives x0..x1 from dLon=lim/(69.172*cos) and y0..y1 from Mercator tileY, with no clamp on ty to [0,2^z) and no wrap on tx, so impossible tiles are really requested; (2) zoomFor (:22) and DETAIL_SPECS (:247-248) choose zoom from range only, so the header comment's '2-9 at any radius' is false (even Chicago 50 mi = 39 base tiles); (3) tiles are awaited one at a time inside the double loop with no per-build cap and no token check, so a superseded build (applyPlace :169 bumps placeToken, ensureDetail :137 bumps detailToken) only has its *result* discarded (:186, :141) -- the fetch stream itself runs to completion, and stepMap's 700 ms debounce (:407) does not prevent several streams overlapping; (4) getBytes (live.mjs:44-61) falls through to the native bridge on any non-200, so each impossible/404 tile costs two round trips with up to 10 s + 12 s timeouts; (5) makePlace (place.mjs:42) accepts |lat| <= 85. confirmed.title: A single failed tile (timeout, 5xx, 429, oversize) is indistinguishable from an empty tile: the map is saved with a hole for 30 days
confirmed.trigger: During buildMap or buildDetail, one tile request out of N fails transiently (OpenFreeMap CDN 5xx, a 10 s timeout on the stick's Wi-Fi, or the native 2 MB cap returning 'oversize'). getBytes resolves null for every non-200 and for timeouts (live.mjs:45, :53, :50); eachTile does `if(!bytes)continue;` and the build only throws when fetched===0 (:185, :316).
confirmed.impact: The base map or detail map is built with a missing quadrant (roads/water/airports in that tile absent; `airports` is also passed to the feed at app.mjs:166/180) and persisted by saveMap/saveDetail; savedMap/savedDetail then serve it for MAX_AGE = 30 days. The applyPlace retry loop (app.mjs:183-197) never runs because the build succeeded. Because there is no in-app cache deletion (known), the only way to recover is to change location or wait 30 days. Transient errors on a free CDN are routine, so this will happen in the field.
confirmed.evidence: mapgen.mjs:94-96: `const bytes=await net.getBytes(...); if(!bytes)continue; fetched++;`  live.mjs:44-46: `const r=await fetch(url,...); if(r.status===200)return new Uint8Array(await r.arrayBuffer());` then bridge: `resolve(status===200?...:null)`; timeout path `setTimeout(()=>{pending.delete(id);resolve(null);},timeoutMs+2000)`. mapgen.mjs:185: `if(!fetched)throw new Error('no tiles');`
confirmed.fix: Make getBytes return a distinguishable result (e.g. {status,bytes}) and treat 204/404 as 'empty tile' but anything else (timeout, connection_error, 429, 5xx, oversize) as a failure: retry that tile once or twice with back-off, and if it still fails either throw (so applyPlace's retry loop runs and nothing partial is saved) or mark the map `partial:true` with a short MAX_AGE so it is rebuilt soon.
reasons:
UPHELD: Confirmed by reading the full path; no refutation found.

Evidence:
- web/live.mjs:41-57 `getBytes`: plain fetch returns bytes only on status 200; any other status, abort/timeout or exception falls through to the bridge; the bridge callback resolves `status===200 ? bytes : null`, and the bridge timer resolves null. src/App.tsx:79-89 maps every non-200, and bodies over MAX_BYTES, to a non-200 status ('oversize' or the HTTP code). So timeout, 5xx, 429, connection error, oversize and a genuinely empty/404/204 tile all collapse to `null`.
- web/mapgen.mjs:93-96 `eachTile`: `if(!bytes)continue; fetched++;` -- no per-tile retry, no record of which tiles were skipped, no expected-vs-fetched comparison.
- web/mapgen.mjs:185 and :316: `if(!fetched)throw new Error('no tiles')` -- the build only fails when every tile is missing.
- web/app.mjs:183-197 `applyPlace`: `saveMap(m)` runs on any resolved build; the back-off retry loop runs only on a throw. web/app.mjs:139-142 `ensureDetail` likewise calls `saveDetail(built)` unconditionally on success.
- web/mapgen.mjs:15,213-217,355-359: savedMap/savedDetail serve the stored object for MAX_AGE = 30 days with no partial flag or completeness check. No in-app cache clear exists (grep shows none).
- Tile counts are small (computed with zoomFor at lat 40: ~6 tiles at 10/20 mi, ~4 at 40 mi, ~9 at 80 mi), so one skipped tile is a quarter to a sixth of the base map -- a conspicuous blank sector, and `airports` from that tile are also absent from the feed passed at app.mjs:166/180.

The `continue` on null is clearly intentional for coverage-edge/empty tiles (OpenFreeMap returns 204/404 there), which is why the status conflation matters: the code cannot tell a legitimately empty ocean tile from a 10 s Wi-Fi timeout on the stick. Tests (node --test) do not exercise a mixed null/ok tile set.

Severity: P2 stands. Not a crash and not data loss, but a routine transient CDN/Wi-Fi failure during the one-time build persists a visibly broken map for 30 days with no user-facing recovery other than changing location. Suggested fix as in the claim: have getBytes return {status, bytes}; treat 204/404 as empty, retry anything else per tile once or twice, and on persistent failure throw (so applyPlace's existing retry loop runs) or save with partial:true and a short expiry.

UPHELD: Confirmed from the code. web/live.mjs:44-57 getBytes collapses every outcome except 200 into null: non-200 plain fetch (falls through), fetch throw/abort, bridge non-200 (including the native 'oversize' and 'connection_error' statuses from src/App.tsx:79-89), and the bridge timeout (`setTimeout(()=>{pending.delete(id);resolve(null);},timeoutMs+2000)`). web/mapgen.mjs:94-96 does `if(!bytes)continue; fetched++;` with no record of which tiles were skipped, and both buildMap (:185) and buildDetail (:316) throw only when fetched===0. UPHELD: Core mechanism confirmed in code. web/mapgen.mjs:94-96 skips any tile for which net.getBytes resolves null, and the build only fails when fetched===0 (:185 for buildMap, :316 for buildDetail). web/live.mjs:41-57 getBytes collapses every non-200 status, abort/timeout, connection error and the native 'oversize' reply (src/App.tsx:79-89) into null, indistinguishable from a legitimately absent tile. No recovery path exists in-app: re-confirming the same place does not rebuild (app.mjs choosePlace, `changed` false), and the only store.remove calls are for HISTORY_KEY (app.mjs:171, :324). The tolerance of null tiles is intentional (tests/test-whatsup.mjs:37,60 feed null for every tile but one, for ocean/empty tiles), which is why a status distinction rather than a blanket throw is the right fix. At 10 mi / z10 the base map is typically 2x2 tiles (tile ~24 mi wide), so one lost tile is a whole missing quadrant of roads, water and places on the main radar for a month. Two corrections that soften but do not refute it: (1) getBytes already makes two attempts per tile (direct WebView fetch with 10 s timeout, then the native bridge with 10+2 s), so a single one-off 5xx/timeout has to repeat to lose the tile; whether the direct fetch even works from file:// on Vega is not determinable statically, so worst case is one attempt. The 'oversize' and 429 triggers are also unlikely for OpenFreeMap z6-z12 tiles. Net: a persistent, user-visible, unrecoverable-for-30-days map hole on a plausible transient failure, but cosmetic and with partial built-in retry, so P2 stands (borderline P3). Suggested fix as claimed: return {status,bytes} from getBytes, treat 204/404 as empty, retry other failures with back-off, and on persistent failure throw or save with a short TTL.

confirmed.title: In-flight street-map build is discarded (not saved, not restarted) when the place object is replaced without moving >111 m; 'Drawing the street map…' note sticks
confirmed.trigger: Default layout is atlas-dark (place.mjs:71), a detail layout, so after confirming a location ensureDetail starts a build that takes a while on the stick (40 tiles even in Chicago at 10 mi). While it is running: open Settings > Adjust position and press OK (the confirm screen itself tells the user to do this), having moved 0-2 presses (<111 m), or re-confirm the same search result. endAdjust/choosePlace always create a new place object (`choosePlace({...a.place,...})`, `settings={...settings,place}`); since `changed` is false (threshold .001°), only refreshLayout() runs.
confirmed.impact: ensureDetail's guard `settings.place!==place` is an identity check, so the finished build is thrown away before saveDetail and before `setText('layout-note','')`; `finally` resets detailBusy but nothing calls ensureDetail again (its only callers are useLayout :119 and applyPlace :179, and applyPlace is skipped). Result: the tiles were downloaded for nothing, the layout stays on the base map with the note 'Drawing the street map…' permanently (no other code path clears layout-note until a map radius or layout change), and the detail map is not persisted. The same discard happens on Adjust-OK with a >111 m move only if maps.detail was already set; when it was still building, applyPlace's keepDetail is false and it restarts, so only the small-move / same-place path is stuck.
confirmed.evidence: app.mjs:141: `if(token!==detailToken||settings.place!==place)return;` app.mjs:212-216: `const changed=!settings.place||Math.abs(settings.place.latitude-place.latitude)>.001||...; settings={...settings,place,confirmed:true}; ... if(changed)applyPlace(place,{fresh:true});else refreshLayout();` app.mjs:218: `function refreshLayout(){try{active?.mod.refresh?.();}catch(e){...}if(lastModel)draw(lastModel);}` (no ensureDetail). Note set at :138, cleared only at :144/:147-148 inside the success/error paths that the early return skips.
confirmed.fix: Compare by coordinates with the same ~.01° tolerance savedDetail uses (`Math.abs(settings.place.latitude-place.latitude)<.01 && ...`) instead of object identity; if the place really changed, re-call ensureDetail after the discard (or have choosePlace's `else` branch call ensureDetail when active.mod.map==='detail' && !maps.detail); clear 'layout-note' on every exit path.

confirmed.title: localStorage quota failure while saving maps is silent and self-defeating: the existing good map in the slot is deleted, nothing is evicted, and maps are rebuilt from tiles on every launch and every return to a detail layout
confirmed.trigger: Any detail or base map whose JSON does not fit alongside the rest (~4.3 MB already measured near the ~5 MB WebView quota per the known list; code comment :238-240 records 6 MB for one 15-mi detail map variant; at Anchorage/Reykjavik/Tromsø the detail map is 2-4x the Chicago tile count, see the tile-count finding). Also reachable by stepping to a wider radius whose map is larger than the previous one.
confirmed.impact: saveDetail catches the QuotaExceededError and *removes the key*, so a previously saved good map in the same slot (e.g. the r10 wide map when the r15 save fails, both live in 'whatsup.detail.v1.wide') is lost. store.set for the base map swallows the error too (live.mjs:63) and `recent` was already updated. No other key is evicted to make room and nothing is logged or shown. confirmed.title: WebView crash or load failure leaves a black screen with keep-awake and engagement still asserted; no watchdog, no retry, and no splash fallback if neither onLoad nor onError fires
confirmed.trigger: The page runs in a separate renderer process (manifest wants com.amazon.webview.renderer_service). Repro paths: (1) renderer killed under memory pressure (TESTING.md shows free RAM dipping to 251 MB while building wide maps) or the page JS halting after load; (2) file:///pkg/assets/index.html fails to load (onError fires); (3) the renderer service never starts (neither onLoad nor onError). The Vega WebView API exposes no renderer-gone callback (WebViewTypes.d.ts prop list: onLoad, onLoadStart, onError, onHttpError, onCloseWindow, onPermissionRequest, onShouldStartLoadWithRequest, onClientCertAuthentication, onSslError) and App.tsx has no heartbeat from the page.
confirmed.impact: Observed: in (1) polling stops and the screen goes black, but `awake && active` remain true so the silent loop keeps playing and KeepAwake.start() keeps being re-asserted every 4 min (App.tsx:128-133) -> the TV shows a dead black screen indefinitely with the screensaver suppressed, until the user notices and relaunches. In (2) the splash is hidden (App.tsx:251) and the user is left on a blank WebView with no message or retry; Back exits because overlayRef is false. In (3) usePreventHideSplashScreen keeps the splash up forever (no timeout). Expected: the host detects a dead page and reloads it, releases keep-awake while nothing is shown, and never leaves the splash or a blank view without a path forward.
confirmed.evidence: App.tsx:237-253: `<WebView ... onLoad={() => hideSplashScreenCallback()} onError={({nativeEvent:{code,url,description}}) => { console.error(...); hideSplashScreenCallback(); }} />` — the only lifecycle handling. App.tsx:147-153: `if (awake && active) { startLoop(); } else { stopLoop(); }` depends solely on AppState and the page's 'awake' message, never on page liveness. App.tsx:120-121: `usePreventHideSplashScreen(); const hideSplashScreenCallback = useHideSplashScreenCallback();` with no timer fallback. Page side: web/live.mjs poll() sends only 'get' requests; there is no periodic liveness message.
confirmed.fix: Have the page post `{type:'alive'}` on every poll tick (web/live.mjs poll(), ~5-15 s). In App.tsx keep `lastAliveRef`; a 60-90 s interval that sees no heartbeat while `active` calls `webRef.current?.reload()` and sets a `pageAlive` state false, which gates `startLoop()`/`engage(true)` alongside `awake && active`. In onError render a native fallback View ("Couldn't load What's Up — press OK to retry") whose OK calls reload(). Add a 15 s setTimeout after mount that calls hideSplashScreenCallback() if onLoad/onError have not fired. Cover with a jest case: no heartbeat -> reload called and KeepAwake.stop() called.
reasons: UPHELD: Code facts verified. ~/overhead-tv/whatsup/src/App.tsx:237-253 is the only WebView lifecycle handling: onLoad -> hideSplashScreenCallback(), onError -> console.error + hideSplashScreenCallback(); no fallback UI, no retry, no timer. App.tsx:120-121 uses usePreventHideSplashScreen()/useHideSplashScreenCallback() with no timeout, so if neither callback fires the splash stays up. App.tsx:124-143 engage(active) + 4-min re-assert and App.tsx:146-152 startLoop()/stopLoop() are gated solely on AppState and the page's 'awake' message (default awake=true at App.tsx:117), with no notion of page liveness. grep over src/ and web/*.mjs finds no 'alive'/heartbeat message and no reload path; node_modules/@amazon-devices/webview/dist/types/WebViewTypes.d.ts lists no renderer-gone callback (onLoad, onLoadStart, onError, onHttpError, onMessage, onCloseWindow, onPermissionRequest, onShouldStartLoadWithRequest, onClientCertAuthentication, onSslError), and manifest.toml:47 does want com.amazon.webview.renderer_service, so the page runs out-of-process. So the three failure paths are real code paths and the claimed consequences (black screen with keep-awake + silent loop still asserted; blank view after onError with Back exiting since overlayRef is false; splash forever) follow from the code. However: (a) none of the paths has been observed -- TESTING.md shows an 18+ min soak with 339-373 MB free and a 251 MB minimum while building maps, with no renderer crash, and the page is a bundled file:///pkg asset so onError in the field is unlikely; (b) the suggested fix calls webRef.current?.reload(), but WebViewMethods in WebViewTypes.d.ts:429-470 exposes no reload() (only goBack/goForward/clearHistory/stopLoading/scrollBy/injectJavaScript/clearCache/dispatchTouchEvent/...), so a recovery would have to remount the WebView (e.g. bump a React key) or re-set source. Real robustness gap with no reproduction, so downgraded to P3; the heartbeat-gated keep-awake and a splash/onError fallback are still worth adding before shipping, using remount rather than reload().

UPHELD: Code facts in the claim check out; I could not find any guard, caller, or default that handles a dead or failed page.

No fallback UI, no retry, no reload call anywhere in src/ (grep for reload/alive/heartbeat/renderer in src/ and web/*.mjs returns nothing relevant).
- Lines 123-144: engagement is driven by a closure-local `active` from AppState only; the 4-minute re-assert interval (128-133) calls engage(false)/engage(true) regardless of page state.
- Lines 147-153: startLoop()/stopLoop() depend only on `awake` (set solely by the page's 'awake' message, line 188-191, default true at line 117) and `active`. Nothing ever sets awake=false if the page stops talking.
- Lines 120-121: usePreventHideSplashScreen() with no timer fallback; if neither onLoad nor onError fires the splash stays up indefinitely.
- Line 163-171: Back returns false (exits) when overlayRef is false, so after an onError the user sits on a black WebView with no message.
- Page side: web/live.mjs only posts {type:'get'} (lines 30, 55); web/app.mjs tellApp posts ui/awake/chime. No periodic liveness message.
- Vega WebView props (node_modules/@amazon-devices/webview/dist/types/WebViewTypes.d.ts ~341-405): onLoad, onLoadStart, onError, onHttpError, onMessage, onCloseWindow, onPermissionRequest, onShouldStartLoadWithRequest, onClientCertAuthentication — no renderer-gone / process-terminated callback, so the host genuinely cannot learn of a renderer death without a page heartbeat.
- manifest.toml:47 wants com.amazon.webview.renderer_service (separate renderer process), consistent with the premise.
- The suggested fix is feasible: although WebViewMethods (WebViewTypes.d.ts:429+) does not declare reload(), the Kepler component implements it (node_modules/@amazon-devices/webview/dist/components/WebView.kepler.js:137 `reload: () => ... Commands.reload(...)`), and webRef is typed `any`, so webRef.current?.reload() works.

Why I lower severity to P3 rather than keep P2: the "Observed" impact in the claim is inferred, not observed. TESTING.md shows the app PASSing wide-map builds at 251-253 MB free with memory steady for 18+ minute sessions, and contains no record of a renderer crash, black screen, or stuck splash. Trigger (2) is a packaged file:///pkg/assets/index.html failing to load, which is very unlikely for a bundled asset, and trigger (3) requires the platform's renderer service to never start, which is outside the app's control and also unobserved. The underlying resilience gap is real and concrete (no watchdog, keep-awake asserted independent of page liveness, no error UI/retry, no splash timeout), and the fix is cheap and low-risk, so it is worth doing before ship — but as a hardening item with hypothetical triggers, not a reproduced defect. If a renderer crash is ever observed in the field, it becomes P2 because the TV would sit on a dead black screen with the screensaver suppressed until the user relaunches.

REFUTED: The code reading is accurate but the claimed impact and severity are not realistic for this app. Verified: App.tsx:237-253 has only onLoad/onError; keep-awake/silent loop are gated only on `awake && active` (App.tsx:128-133, 147-153); usePreventHideSplashScreen has no timeout; the Vega WebView prop surface has no renderer-gone callback and the page posts no heartbeat (web/live.mjs only sends 'get'). However, none of the three trigger paths is evidence-backed: (1) No renderer crash has ever been observed. TESTING.md records the stick at 18+ min continuous, 250 mi with ~300 aircraft, satellite/wide-map builds, and idle runs with free RAM never below 251 MB and recovering to 350+ MB after each build; 251 MB free is a transient low on a device with ~2 GB, not an OOM. The 'memory pressure kills the renderer' scenario is speculation with no repro. (2) file:///pkg/assets/index.html is a packaged asset; scripts/build-web.mjs:62-65 throws if index.html lacks the script tag, and a missing packaged file would fail on the very first QA launch of any build, not in the field. (3) 'renderer service never starts' is hypothetical with no observation. The impact is also overstated: 'dead black screen indefinitely, no path forward' is wrong because the BackHandler returns false when overlayRef is false (App.tsx:163-166), so Back exits the app immediately, and Home always works; the user is one key press from recovery, and keep-awake on a black screen causes no harm beyond the screensaver not appearing. Note also that the suggested fix calls `webRef.current?.reload()`, which is not in the Vega WebView ref API (WebViewTypes.d.ts exposes goBack, stopLoading, injectJavaScript); a remount via a `key` bump would be needed. Residual value: a page heartbeat + remount and a splash timeout are reasonable long-running-display hardening, but with no observed failure and trivial user recovery this is P3 hardening, not a P2 ship blocker.

confirmed.title: silentLoop start/stop/start race: a start that lands during the first player's post-init deinitialize returns the stale promise, leaving wanted=true with no player and no retry (harness-confirmed)
confirmed.trigger: `awake && active` goes true -> false -> true within the window between the first VideoPlayer's initialize() callback and the completion of its deinitialize() destroy callback (two native round-trips, tens to a few hundred ms). Realistic: two quick OK presses on Settings > Keep screen awake (Off then On, App.tsx setAwake -> effect), or an AppState active->inactive->active flap. Exact sequence: startLoop() creates S1 (awaiting p1.initialize()); stopLoop() sets wanted=false (player still null, nothing to pause); p1 init resolves, `!wanted` branch awaits p1.deinitialize(); meanwhile startLoop() sets wanted=true, sees player===null and `starting` non-null, and returns S1; S1 finishes the deinit and resolves; finally sets starting=null. Nothing calls startLoop() again until the next awake/active change. Reproduced with a timing mock of the w3cmedia MediaPlayer (async init/destroy callbacks, immediate play()) in the scratchpad: output `p1 init-done`, `p1 deinit`, 1 player created, none ever played.
confirmed.impact: Observed: the switch reads On, the engagement report is still made, but no media plays, so Vega's screensaver returns after its normal idle timeout (TESTING.md: engagement alone fails at ~5 min). Expected: after the last startLoop() call with wanted=true, a loop is playing.
confirmed.evidence: src/silentLoop.ts:24-29: `wanted = true; if (player) return Promise.resolve(); if (!starting) { starting = (async () => { ... })() ... } return starting;` and :39-42: `if (!wanted) { await p.deinitialize(); return; }` — the `!wanted` branch never re-checks `wanted` after the await, and a concurrent startLoop() only re-uses `starting`. Harness: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-the owner-Documents-ChatGPT-Vibe-Coding/2afc01d9-34cf-4185-ae38-d85a302dd1ae/scratchpad/loop/harness.js (transpiled copy of silentLoop.ts; the repo was not modified).
confirmed.fix: After the deinitialize in the `!wanted` branch, re-check and restart: `if (!wanted) { await p.deinitialize(); if (wanted && !player) { starting = null; return startLoop(); } return; }`; or in startLoop, when `starting` exists, return `starting.then(() => (wanted && !player && !starting ? startLoop() : undefined))`. Add a jest case with fake timers that toggles start/stop/start across the init/deinit boundary and asserts play() was called on a live player.
reasons: UPHELD: Confirmed against the code and by re-running the race on an independent transpiled copy of ~/overhead-tv/whatsup/src/silentLoop.ts with a timing mock (async initialize/deinitialize, 50 ms each): sequence startLoop() -> stopLoop() (before init resolves) -> startLoop() (after init resolved, during deinit) produced only `p1 init-done`, `p1 deinit`; no player was ever created or played, and afterwards `wanted===true`, `player===null`, `starting===null`. Mechanism is exactly as claimed: startLoop (lines 24-29) returns the in-flight `starting` promise when `player` is null, and the `!wanted` branch (lines 39-42) never re-checks `wanted` after `await p.deinitialize()`, so the second start is silently dropped. Caller analysis confirms nothing retries: the only drivers are the App.tsx `[awake, active]` effect (lines 147-153), fed by the page's `awake` message (web/app.mjs:343 sends one per OK press on Settings > Keep screen awake, :389 on settings reset, :656 on load) and the AppState listener (lines 134-138); no timer or periodic re-assert calls startLoop. One correction to the claim: the vulnerable window is narrower than "two native round-trips" -- a start that lands while initialize() is still pending is safe because line 39 reads `wanted` synchronously after init resolves; only a start landing between that check and the completion of deinitialize() is lost (one native round-trip, tens of ms). The trigger therefore requires a fast Off->On double-press or an AppState active->inactive->active flap inside that window, which is uncommon but real. Impact matches TESTING.md:83 (engagement alone fails at ~5 min; the silent loop is what holds off the screensaver), and the switch would read On while nothing plays until the next awake/active transition self-heals it. P3 is the right severity: narrow timing window, self-corrects on the next toggle or background/foreground cycle, no crash or data impact. Suggested fix in the claim (re-check `wanted` after the deinit await and restart, or chain a re-check onto the returned `starting` promise) is correct.

The sequence startLoop -> stopLoop -> startLoop, with the third call landing after p1.initialize() resolves but before the `!wanted` branch's `await p.deinitialize()` (line 40) completes, leaves wanted=true, player=null, starting=null with no player ever played: the second startLoop sees player===null and `starting` non-null (line 29) and just returns the in-flight promise; the `!wanted` branch returns without re-checking `wanted` after the await; `.finally` clears `starting`. Trigger is plausible (two quick OK presses on the Keep-awake switch, or an active->inactive->active AppState flap), but the window is narrow (one deinitialize round-trip) and the consequence is the screensaver returning after its normal ~5 min timeout until the next awake/active change, so P3 is the right severity.

In ~/overhead-tv/whatsup/src/silentLoop.ts:24-55, a startLoop() that arrives while `starting` is non-null only returns the existing promise (line 54) and never re-checks `wanted`; the `!wanted` branch at :39-42 awaits p.deinitialize() and returns without looking at `wanted` again. My mock run (async 50 ms init/deinit) printed `p1 new / p1 init-done / p1 deinit`, played: false. The caller in App.tsx:147-153 only calls startLoop()/stopLoop() from the [awake, active] effect, and nothing else (not the 4-min engage() reassert timer) re-invokes startLoop, so the stuck state persists until the next awake/active change. The trigger is real but narrow: it needs the second toggle to land after init completes but before deinit completes (not merely before init completes; in that case line 39 sees wanted=true and plays correctly), i.e. a fast double OK on Settings > Keep screen awake or an AppState active->inactive->active flap within tens to a few hundred ms. Suggested fix in the claim (re-check `wanted` after the deinit await and restart, or chain a re-check onto the returned `starting`) is correct and small. P3 is the right severity: real, reproducible logic bug, but requires tight timing on a non-default-risk path and degrades to the pre-feature behaviour rather than a crash or data loss.

confirmed.title: ADSB.lol route cache stores unbounded airport name/location strings: a hostile route server fills WebView memory (≈190 MB in 6 min, >1 GB/h) and localStorage
confirmed.trigger: Any 200 reply from vrs-standing-data.adsb.lol whose `_airports[i].name` / `.location` are long strings (the bridge allows up to 2 MB). `slim()` (live.mjs:198) keeps `name` and `location` verbatim; Enricher.tick stores the result for 1 h at `L.put('lol:'+call, data, now+HOUR)` (live.mjs:262), one new callsign every poll (5 s cooldown). The entry is held in the in-memory Ledger Map and re-stringified by `store.set(LEDGER_KEY,ledger)` on every dirty tick.
confirmed.impact: Measured with node against web/live.mjs: 60 polls with a 1.9 MB-class payload (12 airports x 150 KB names) -> 241 ledger rows, ledger JSON 216 MB, heap +190 MB, and `JSON.stringify(ledger)` costs 89 ms per tick (desktop; several x slower on the stick). Linear growth to ~720 entries/h (~1.4 GB at the 2 MB cap) -> WebView OOM; before that, every 5 s tick serialises hundreds of MB (UI stalls) and localStorage writes of the ledger fail silently so no routes persist. Only names/locations that reach the display are sliced (commercialRoute `place()` 80/40), the cached copy is not.
confirmed.evidence: const slim=p=>({callsign:p.callsign,_airports:Array.isArray(p._airports)?p._airports.slice(0,12).map(x=>({iata:x?.iata,icao:x?.icao,name:x?.name,location:x?.location,lat:x?.lat,lon:x?.lon})):[]});  // probe: 'requests 60 ledger rows 241 ledger JSON bytes 216.1 MB heap delta 190 MB; JSON.stringify(ledger) 89 ms'
confirmed.fix: In `slim`, coerce and cap every field: `name:String(x?.name||'').slice(0,80), location:String(x?.location||'').slice(0,40), iata/icao via ident()`, `lat/lon` only if finite; additionally refuse to cache a slimmed payload above a few KB (`JSON.stringify(data).length>4096 -> store {}` as a miss), and cap the number of `lol:` rows (e.g. drop oldest beyond 200).
reasons: UPHELD: The code path is real and reproduces. web/live.mjs:198 `slim()` copies `name`/`location` from the ADSB.lol payload verbatim (only `_airports` is capped at 12); Enricher.tick (live.mjs:255-263) stores the slimmed object at `lol:<callsign>` for 1 h; the only size gate is the native bridge's MAX_BYTES = 2 MiB per reply (src/App.tsx:34,89), so each cached row can be ~1.8 MB. Every live aircraft within searchNm (default 15 nm, widened by `reach`, up to MAX_NM=250) with an airline-style callsign is enqueued (observations() has no count cap; `free` is unbounded), one new callsign fetched per 5 s cooldown. The whole Ledger is re-stringified by `store.set(LEDGER_KEY,ledger)` (live.mjs:298) on every dirty tick, and the localStorage write fails silently (store.set catch) once the quota is exceeded, so no routes persist. Reproduction with node against web/live.mjs (Enricher with a stub request returning 12 airports x 150 KB names): 60 ticks -> 61 ledger rows, ledger JSON 108 MB, heap +109 MB, JSON.stringify 91 ms per tick on desktop. Growth is linear until the 1 h expiry, so busy airspace (dozens to hundreds of distinct callsigns/h) drives a Fire TV WebView to hundreds of MB and OOM, with multi-hundred-ms main-thread stalls each poll before that. Only the display copy is sliced (commercialRoute `place()` 80/40 at live.mjs:190-191); the cached copy is not. Severity adjusted to P2 rather than P1: the trigger requires a compromised or MITM'd vrs-standing-data.adsb.lol (real payloads are a few KB, so there is no benign trigger), and the impact is app crash/DoS on the TV, not data exposure. Suggested fix stands: cap/coerce fields in slim() (name 80, location 40, iata/icao via ident(), lat/lon only if finite), treat a slimmed payload above a few KB as a miss, and bound the number of `lol:` rows.

UPHELD: Mechanism confirmed in code, impact overstated. web/live.mjs:198 `slim()` copies `name`/`location` verbatim (only `_airports` is capped at 12 entries); the only truncation (`place()` at live.mjs:190-191, 80/40 chars) applies to the published route, not the cached copy. live.mjs:261-262 stores the slimmed payload under `lol:<callsign>` for 1 h whenever `payload.callsign===call`, one new callsign per tick subject to the 5 s cooldown (live.mjs:256), and `Ledger.put` (live.mjs:207-210) only evicts expired rows, so there is no count or byte cap. src/App.tsx:34/84/89 lets up to 2 MB per reply through the bridge. `store.set` (live.mjs:63) swallows the localStorage quota error, so once the ledger JSON exceeds ~5 MB nothing new persists and every dirty tick (any sighting/cooldown put marks dirty) re-stringifies the whole in-memory ledger. So a hostile/compromised vrs-standing-data.adsb.lol origin can grow WebView heap linearly for an hour before expiry prunes it. Mitigating facts that lower severity: (1) the attacker must control that exact allow-listed HTTPS origin (or its CDN); it is not reachable by any aircraft/feed data or by other services; (2) the damage is a stall/OOM of the TV app only, with no data exposure; (3) persistence is bounded by the localStorage quota and the 1 h row expiry, so a restart recovers (the on-disk ledger is the last write that fit under quota, and poisoned rows expire within the hour); (4) the quota-failure path also degrades gracefully to memory-only. This is a hardening gap against a malicious upstream, not a shipping-blocker. Suggested fix stands: in `slim`, coerce/cap `name` (80) and `location` (40), pass iata/icao through `ident()`, keep lat/lon only if finite, and skip caching payloads whose slimmed JSON exceeds a few KB.

Only the display copy is sliced (live.mjs:189-190), not the cached one. So a hostile vrs-standing-data.adsb.lol can make the in-memory ledger grow ~1.9 MB per new callsign and the ledger stops persisting once the serialised size passes the quota. Two things cut the realistic impact: (1) the precondition is a compromised or hijacked adsb.lol origin/CDN; ROUTE_URL is HTTPS and host-pinned by the App.tsx allow-list (line 24), so no on-path or DNS attacker suffices, and a hobbyist route server going hostile is a supply-chain event affecting every adsb.lol client, not something a TV user triggers; (2) growth is bounded by distinct live callsigns in the search area per hour (each is fetched once and cached 1 h), not by the 5 s cooldown, so the realistic rate is tens to a couple hundred entries/hour, i.e. hundreds of MB over an evening near a hub rather than 1.4 GB/h. The outcome is a WebView stall/OOM crash and lost route persistence while the upstream stays hostile; no data exposure, no persistent corruption (the last successfully saved ledger is small, and entries expire in 1 h). That is a real robustness gap against an untrusted upstream with a two-line fix (cap name/location in `slim`, bound `lol:` row count/size), but it is a hardening item, not a ship-blocking P1 for a home TV app.

confirmed.title: Quadratic regex on feed `ownOp` (titleCase / airlineAlts): a crafted owner string freezes every poll for minutes
confirmed.trigger: Feed entry with an unknown airline prefix (callsign e.g. `ZZZ1` or a registration) and `ownOp` = N whitespace chars followed by a non-matching tail. `enrich()` (model.mjs:166-167) calls `titleCase(owner)` for every such plane on every tick (up to MAX_PLANES=300); Radar/Cockpit also call `kit.airlineAlts(hero.operator)` (kit.mjs:99-100) on every render. Neither input is length-capped (`owner=r.ownOp.trim()`), the bridge allows 2 MB of feed JSON.
confirmed.impact: The patterns `[,.]?\s+(inc|co|...)\.?$` and `[\s,]+(S\.?A\.?...)$` backtrack O(N^2). Measured in node: 40k spaces -> 0.8 s, 100k -> 4.6 s, 200k -> 18.8 s per call (desktop V8). Ten such aircraft in one 2 MB feed = minutes of main-thread block per 5-second poll, for as long as the feed stays hostile; remote keys are dead during the block.
confirmed.evidence: model.mjs:52 const titleCase=s=>s.toLowerCase().replace(/[,.]?\s+(inc|co|llc|ltd|corp|corporation|company|plc|gmbh|sa|ag)\.?$/,'')...  model.mjs:167 (owner&&!/BANK|.../i.test(owner)?titleCase(owner):'')  // probe: titleCase(200000 spaces + 'x') 18755 ms
confirmed.fix: Cap and normalise owner before any regex: `owner=typeof r.ownOp==='string'?r.ownOp.trim().slice(0,80):''` (and collapse runs of whitespace with `.replace(/\s+/g,' ')`). Same cap at the top of `airlineAlts`. Optionally rewrite the suffix regexes to anchor on a single separator (`(?:^|[\s,])(inc|co|...)\.?$`) so backtracking is linear.
reasons: UPHELD: Not refuted. Code path verified: src/App.tsx:34,84-89 forwards feed bodies up to 2 MB unchanged; web/model.mjs:210 builds `raw` straight from `payload.ac`; web/model.mjs:162-167 does `owner=r.ownOp.trim()` with no length cap and calls `titleCase(owner)` for every enriched plane whose callsign has no OPERATORS prefix (up to MAX_PLANES=300 per poll); web/kit.mjs:98-100 `airlineAlts(hero.operator)` runs the second backtracking regex on every Radar/Cockpit render (radar.mjs:161, cockpit.mjs:192). Reproduced locally with the exact regexes (Node 24): titleCase 40k spaces = 664 ms, 100k = 4.3 s; airlineAlts 40k = 1.36 s, 100k = 8.75 s, i.e. clearly quadratic, so one 2 MB `ownOp` would freeze the WebView main thread for far longer than a poll cycle, recurring on every poll, on much slower Fire TV hardware. Suggested fix (slice owner to ~80 chars, collapse whitespace, anchor the suffix regex on a single separator) is correct. Severity adjusted down one notch: the trigger requires the adsb.fi origin itself (or a TLS compromise) to serve hostile data, since the bridge only fetches allow-listed HTTPS URLs and genuine ownOp values are short registry strings; impact is availability only (app unusable until feed is clean or app restarts), with no data exposure. Real, cheap-to-fix hardening gap against a trusted upstream, not an externally reachable DoS.

confirmed.title: Planespotters lookups that fail for network reasons are cached as 'no photo' for 24 hours
confirmed.trigger: Connection drops, DNS fails, the 3 s (+2 s bridge) timeout fires, or Planespotters returns 429/5xx/HTML while an aircraft is the current one. photoFor resolves null for status!==200 and stores that promise in `cache` keyed by hex with a 24 h TTL.
confirmed.impact: After the network recovers, every aircraft first seen during the outage shows no photo (falls back to the bundled model photo or nothing) until 24 h pass or 300 other aircraft evict it. On a TV watching the same local traffic (recurring commuter flights, based GA aircraft) this is a visible, long-lived regression from a transient blip. A genuine 404 'no photo' should be cached; a timeout/429/connection_error should not be.
confirmed.evidence: photos.mjs:35-41 `const promise=(async()=>{ let {status,payload}=await getJson(PHOTO_URL('hex',hex),3000); let photo=status===200?parsePhoto(payload):null; ... return photo; })().catch(()=>null); cache.set(hex,{at:Date.now(),promise});` and :33 `if(hit&&Date.now()-hit.at<DAY)return hit.promise;` — the cached entry is identical for a 200-with-no-photos and for 'connection_error'/429/'invalid'.
confirmed.fix: Return {photo,status} from the inner function and only cache for DAY when status===200 or 404; for connection_error/timeout/'invalid'/429/5xx either don't cache or cache with a short TTL (e.g. 60 s, 15 min on 429) so the lookup is retried once the aircraft is shown again.
reasons: UPHELD: Confirmed by code and by a live repro. web/photos.mjs:35-41 stores the promise in `cache` keyed by hex unconditionally, and :33 returns it for 24 h; the inner async resolves null for any non-200 status (and `.catch(()=>null)` for throws). web/live.mjs:21-37 never throws and maps timeouts/aborts/DNS failures to {status:'connection_error'} (bridge path :28/:30, browser path :35; src/App.tsx:89-91 returns 'connection_error' for native fetch failures, and non-200 codes such as 429/5xx pass through as the numeric status). So a transient failure produces the same cached null as a genuine "no photos" 200. Repro (node, fetch stubbed): first photoFor({hex:'a1b2c3',registration:'N123AB'}) with fetch throwing -> null, 1 call; second photoFor with fetch returning a valid photo -> still null, still 1 call (no refetch). Callers web/kit.mjs:43 (showPhotoIn) and web/layouts/atlas.mjs:221 then fall back to the bundled model photo or nothing. Mitigations: the cache is an in-memory Map (cleared on app restart/page reload), capped at 300 entries, and the degradation is cosmetic with a model-photo fallback, so I rate this P3 rather than P2: a long-running TV session after a Wi-Fi blip shows no Planespotters photo for aircraft first seen during the blip, for up to 24 h. Suggested fix stands: cache for DAY only when the final status is 200 or 404; for 'connection_error'/'invalid'/429/5xx don't cache (or use a short TTL).

UPHELD: Confirmed in code. web/photos.mjs:35-41: the inner async resolves `photo=null` whenever `status!==200` (getJson in web/live.mjs:21-36 returns 'connection_error' on bridge timeout/postMessage failure/fetch rejection, 'invalid' on bad JSON, and raw HTTP status for 404/429/5xx), the outer `.catch(()=>null)` swallows anything else, and the promise is stored unconditionally in `cache` with `at:Date.now()`; :33 returns that cached null for 24 h without distinguishing failure from a genuine no-photo result. Nothing elsewhere compensates: the two callers (web/kit.mjs:43 showPhotoIn and web/layouts/atlas.mjs:221 showPhoto) call photoFor only when the shown hex changes and simply fall through to modelPhoto/nothing on null, so a re-shown aircraft gets the cached null again; there is no cache invalidation on network recovery. Mitigating factors that lower severity rather than refute: the cache is an in-memory Map (not localStorage), so it is per-WebView-session only (comment at :9 says so); entries are FIFO-evicted past 300; during an outage only the aircraft actually looked up while it lasted are poisoned (typically the few that were current); and the visible effect is a fallback to the bundled model photo or no picture, never an error. A long-running TV session with recurring local traffic does make the degradation observable for up to 24 h. Suggested fix stands: have the inner function return {photo,status} and only cache for DAY on status 200/404, skipping or short-TTL caching for 'connection_error'/'invalid'/429/5xx.

UPHELD: Confirmed in code. web/photos.mjs:35-41: the inner async resolves null for any status!==200 (getJson in web/live.mjs:21-36 maps bridge timeout, fetch rejection and App.tsx:64-94 fetch failures to 'connection_error', non-200 HTTP to the numeric status, bad JSON to 'invalid'), the trailing .catch(()=>null) swallows everything else, and line 41 caches that promise keyed by hex unconditionally; line 33 serves it for DAY (24 h). There is no distinction between a 200-with-empty-photos miss and a failure, so a single 3 s timeout (the most likely trigger on a slow API, not even a full outage), a 429, or a 5xx while an aircraft is the hero pins that aircraft to 'no photo' for the rest of the session. Both callers (web/kit.mjs:43 showPhotoIn, used by the layouts; web/layouts/atlas.mjs:221 showPhoto) only call photoFor when the hero hex changes and otherwise trust the cached promise, so nothing retries. The header comment (photos.mjs:9 'misses too') shows caching misses is intentional, but it does not account for failures.
