Net: real, visible, cosmetic degradation that self-heals on restart. Fix as suggested: return {photo,status} and only cache for DAY on status 200 or 404; skip caching (or use a short TTL) for 'connection_error', 'invalid', 429 and 5xx.

confirmed.title: Orphaned map builds keep fetching after the user moves on: no cancellation, so radius stepping multiplies tile traffic and runs several builds concurrently
confirmed.trigger: Press Up/Down (stepMap) or change Settings > Map radius more than once within a build. Each pause of 700 ms starts applyPlace -> buildMap for the new radius (only the 3 most recent base maps and one 'wide' detail map are saved, so most steps are uncached) and ensureDetail -> buildDetail; the previous build's token is invalidated only after its `await buildMap(...)` resolves, and eachTile has no abort signal, so every tile of the abandoned build is still downloaded (and decoded).
confirmed.impact: Measured tile counts per radius with a mocked net (base + detail): 2 mi 2+28, 5 mi 2+28, 10 mi 4+36, 15 mi 12+56, 25 mi 21+20, 50 mi 39+25, 100 mi 9+20, 150 mi 6+16, 250 mi 12+36, plus one tilejson per build. Walking 10 -> 250 mi and back with short pauses issues roughly 450+ tile requests and 20+ tilejson requests to OpenFreeMap, with up to 9 builds fetching at once (each tile up to 10 s plain + 12 s bridge). Because wide detail maps share a single '.wide' slot, every wide step rebuilds and overwrites the previous one, so stepping back re-fetches it again. Results from the stale builds are discarded on arrival (token mismatch), so the bandwidth is wasted; on a slow link the builds also starve the 5 s feed poll (same bridge). Expected: an abandoned build stops fetching, and stepping through radii costs at most the current radius' tiles.
confirmed.evidence: app.mjs:184-188 `for(let attempt=0;token===placeToken;attempt++){ try{ const m=await buildMap(place,range); if(token!==placeToken)return;` (check only after the whole build); app.mjs:140-141 same pattern for buildDetail; mapgen.mjs:93-96 sequential `await net.getBytes(...)` with no AbortSignal or cancellation flag; app.mjs:407 `mapTimer=setTimeout(()=>{if(settings.place)applyPlace(settings.place);},700);`; mapgen.mjs:354 `const detailKey=spec=>spec.key==='street'?DETAIL_KEY:`${DETAIL_KEY}.wide`;`
confirmed.fix: Pass a cancellation token/AbortSignal into buildMap/buildDetail -> eachTile (check `if(cancelled)throw` before each tile and pass the signal to getBytes/fetch and the bridge timeout), and cancel it in applyPlace/ensureDetail whenever placeToken/detailToken advances. Optionally debounce radius stepping longer (e.g. 1.5 s) and keep more than one wide detail slot.
reasons: UPHELD: Confirmed from code and a mocked-net repro. web/app.mjs:183-186 checks placeToken only after `await buildMap()` resolves, app.mjs:140-141 does the same for buildDetail, and app.mjs:177 resets detailBusy and bumps detailToken so a new detail build starts while the old one still runs. web/mapgen.mjs:93-94 eachTile awaits net.getBytes per tile with no cancellation flag or AbortSignal; live.mjs:41-55 and src/App.tsx:64-92 have only per-request timeouts and no concurrency cap. app.mjs:406-407 fires applyPlace after each 700 ms pause; mapgen.mjs:219-223 keeps 3 base maps and mapgen.mjs:354 one '.wide' detail slot, so most steps are uncached and wide steps overwrite each other. Measured with a mocked net (no network): base+detail tiles per radius 1+28, 2+28, 6+40, 9+50, 18+25, 39+25, 9+25, 9+12, 12+30 plus one tilejson per build (matches the claim within latitude variation); 7 base builds started 1 ms apart reached 7 concurrent in-flight tile fetches with none stopping. Mitigations: detail builds only occur on layouts with mod.map==='detail' (app.mjs:119,179) and only pauses >700 ms trigger a build; feed starvation is plausible but not measured. P2 stands: wasted bandwidth/third-party load and CPU on the stick, no crash or data loss.

UPHELD: Confirmed in code and by a mock-net run. web/mapgen.mjs:86-123 eachTile awaits net.getBytes per tile sequentially with no AbortSignal or cancel flag; buildMap (:126) and buildDetail (:271) expose no cancellation. web/app.mjs:183-186 and :140-141 only compare the token after the whole build resolves, and applyPlace (:169, :177) bumps tokens without stopping in-flight loops; live.mjs getBytes (:41-55) and the App.tsx bridge (:197-215) have only per-request timeouts. stepMap (:398-407) debounces 700 ms but every pause beyond that starts a new applyPlace, and with saveMap keeping 3 radii (:219-224) and a single '.wide' detail slot (:354) most steps are uncached. Repro: three buildMap calls at 25/50/100 mi with a counting mock net ran concurrently (3 in flight) and issued 27 tile fetches with nothing able to stop the stale ones; a 250 mi buildDetail alone issued 30. Mitigations present: debounce, stale builds do not retry after failure (:191), stale results are discarded so no wrong map is shown. Impact is wasted OpenFreeMap traffic, slower arrival of the wanted map and contention with the feed poll on a slow link, not a functional failure, so P3 rather than P2.

UPHELD: Verified against the code; the claim holds. (1) No cancellation: web/mapgen.mjs:86-96 `eachTile` is a sequential `await net.getBytes(...)` loop with no abort signal or cancelled flag; web/live.mjs:41-57 `getBytes` creates its own per-request AbortController only for the timeout. (2) Token checked only after the whole build: web/app.mjs:184-187 (`const m=await buildMap(place,range); if(token!==placeToken)return;`) and app.mjs:139-141 for buildDetail. (3) Concurrent builds are real, not just orphaned: app.mjs:176 `if(!keepDetail){maps.detail=null;detailToken++;detailBusy=false;}` clears the `detailBusy` guard while the previous buildDetail is still running, so app.mjs:178 `ensureDetail()` starts another one; applyPlace itself has no busy guard at all. (4) Trigger is realistic: app.mjs:406-407 fires applyPlace 700 ms after each Up/Down step; a user exploring radii with ~1 s pauses fires one build per step, and the comment at app.mjs:393-395 even advertises stepping as "cheap". (5) Tile counts reproduced with a mock net at a generic city (base/detail): 2mi 1/28, 5mi 2/28, 10mi 6/40, 15mi 9/50, 25mi 18/25, 50mi 39/25, 100mi 9/25, 150mi 9/12, 250mi 12/30, plus a tilejson per build; mapgen.mjs:220-222 keeps only 3 base maps and mapgen.mjs:354 gives all wide detail maps one `.wide` slot, so most steps are cache misses and stepping back re-fetches. Impact on a Fire TV stick is material: besides wasted bandwidth to a free tile service, each orphaned build still decodes every tile synchronously on the WebView main thread (mapgen.mjs:97+), and the codebase itself notes that re-decoding maps "blocked the stick for seconds" (app.mjs:162-163), so several overlapping builds produce seconds of jank/unresponsive remote and delay the map the user actually wants. Results are correctly discarded (no wrong map shown), which is why this stays P2 rather than higher. Bridge requests are not serialized in App.tsx (onMessage fires `get(...)` per request), so feed "starvation" is bandwidth/CPU contention rather than queueing; that nuance does not change the finding. Suggested fix stands: thread a cancel flag/AbortSignal from applyPlace/ensureDetail into buildMap/buildDetail -> eachTile and check it before each tile.

confirmed.title: At wide map radii the adsb.fi payload can exceed the 2 MB bridge cap, leaving the feed permanently dead while the full body is re-downloaded every poll
confirmed.trigger: Settings > Map radius 150 or 250 mi (searchNm = min(250, ceil(1.5*r/1.15078)) = 196 or 250 NM) in a dense corridor (US north-east, Chicago, London/Benelux, Rhine-Main). The fixture tests/fixtures/chicago-feed.json averages 564 bytes per aircraft, so ~3,700 aircraft in the circle crosses MAX_BYTES = 2,097,152 chars; adsb.fi's 250 NM cap is the maximum area and busy hours put the aircraft count in that range. Also hit by checkCoverage (live.mjs:309), which always requests 250 NM.
confirmed.impact: App.tsx get() downloads the whole body, then returns 'oversize'; live.mjs poll treats it as a failure (`onUpdate(states,false)`) and schedules the next poll in pollSeconds (15 s at these radii) with no back-off and no shrinking of the radius. The screen shows a stale/empty sky (Observed) while the device keeps pulling >2 MB every 15 s = >11 GB/day from adsb.fi's free feed with zero benefit, and parsing never happens so the user gets no error beyond 'stale'. Below the cap the same setting still means a 1-2 MB JSON parse every 15 s on a Fire TV stick. Expected: the feed degrades (smaller radius or longer interval) and the cap aborts the download early.
confirmed.evidence: app.mjs:36-38 `searchNm:Math.min(MAX_NM,Math.max(CONFIG.searchNm,Math.ceil(reach/1.15078))), pollSeconds:r<=25?CONFIG.pollSeconds:r<=100?10:15`; src/App.tsx:88-89 `const text = await response.text(); return text.length > MAX_BYTES ? ['oversize', ''] : [200, text];`; live.mjs:315-327 `const {status,payload}=await getJson(FEED_URL(...,config.searchNm),4000); ... }else onUpdate(states,false); timer=setTimeout(poll,Math.max(1000,config.pollSeconds*1000-(Date.now()-started)));`; fixture: 31,003 bytes / 55 aircraft = 564 B each.
confirmed.fix: Treat 'oversize' (and 429/5xx) in poll as a distinct failure: back off (e.g. double the interval up to 60 s) and automatically reduce searchNm (halve, down to the alert-zone reach) until a reply fits, surfacing 'Too much traffic for this radius' in the note. In App.tsx stream the body and abort once Content-Length or bytes read exceed MAX_BYTES instead of after the full download. Consider capping searchNm at ~100 NM regardless of map radius.
reasons: REFUTED: The code path exists exactly as cited (src/App.tsx:88-89 reads the whole body then returns 'oversize'; web/live.mjs:315-327 treats any non-200 as a plain failure and re-polls at config.pollSeconds with no back-off; web/app.mjs:36-38 asks for up to MAX_NM=250 NM at the 150/250 mi radii from MAP_RADII in web/place.mjs:54). But the trigger does not hold up. Hitting the 2,097,152-char cap requires ~3,750 aircraft in one adsb.fi response (fixture tests/fixtures/chicago-feed.json: avg 558 B/aircraft, median 590, max 643). The project's own device testing at 250 mi (TESTING.md:65,84,85) observed ~300 aircraft, and web/model.mjs:209 budgets for "500+" over a busy region; a 250 NM circle even over the US north-east or London/Benelux at peak is on the order of 1,500-3,000 tracked aircraft, well short of ~3,750, and adsb.fi's own 250 NM limit bounds the area. No fixture, log, or test in the repo shows a payload anywhere near 2 MB, so the "permanently dead feed / 11 GB per day" scenario is not demonstrated. The checkCoverage angle is weaker still: live.mjs:321 only calls it when the normal poll returned zero aircraft, and a failed coverage check leaves coverage.none unchanged rather than breaking anything. What remains is a hardening gap, not a reproducible defect: get() in App.tsx could abort on Content-Length/bytes-read instead of after the full download, and poll() could back off on 'oversize'/429/5xx instead of retrying at the same cadence. Worth noting separately (not this claim): the poll uses a 4000 ms bridge timeout (live.mjs:315 -> App.tsx:211-214), so a legitimately large 1-1.5 MB body on a slow stick Wi-Fi link would surface as 'connection_error' and a stale sky before the size cap is ever reached. Downgraded to P3 as a low-priority robustness item without a confirmed failure case.

UPHELD: Not refuted. The code confirms every link in the chain: web/app.mjs:37-38 requests 196/250 NM at 15 s with no traffic-adaptive cap; src/App.tsx:88-89 reads the entire body via response.text() before comparing to MAX_BYTES, so 'oversize' is returned only after a full download (the 4 s abort at App.tsx:70 is the only early stop); web/live.mjs:315-327 treats oversize exactly like any other failure (`else onUpdate(states,false)`) and reschedules at the same searchNm and pollSeconds — grep finds no back-off or oversize handling anywhere in web/*.mjs. model.mjs:208 then flips fresh=false after 15 s and kit.mjs:149-150 shows 'No signal / Retrying every few seconds', which is misleading since it never recovers at that radius. The fixture is genuine adsb.fi v3 shape at ~561 B/aircraft, so the cap is crossed at ~3,740 aircraft; model.mjs:211's own comment assumed only '500+' at 250 mi, so peak density was not budgeted. The one unverifiable premise (adsb.fi returning >3,700 aircraft in 250 NM) is on the margin and only plausible at peak over NW Europe/US NE, but the identical dead-feed-with-no-degradation outcome occurs more easily via the 4 s timeout on a 1-2 MB body (connection_error path, same branch). The 11 GB/day number only applies when downloads complete within 4 s; otherwise waste is bounded to 4 s per poll. checkCoverage is a minor contributor (once per 30 min, only when the normal poll is empty, and an oversize there just leaves coverage.none unchanged). Severity P2 stands: self-inflicted by a wide-radius setting, but the result is a permanently dead feed with a misleading message and continuous wasted downloads against a free third-party feed, with no automatic recovery.

UPHELD: Mechanism confirmed in code, magnitude and framing overstated. Confirmed: web/app.mjs:36-37 sets searchNm = min(250, ceil(1.5*r/1.15078)) so Map radius 150/250 mi requests 196/250 NM with pollSeconds 15; src/App.tsx:88-89 reads the whole body with response.text() and only then returns 'oversize' when text.length > 2,097,152; web/live.mjs:21-31 getJson maps any non-200 status (including 'oversize') to payload:null; live.mjs:315-327 poll() treats that as onUpdate(states,false) and reschedules at the same interval with no back-off, no radius reduction and no user-facing reason (core.mjs:25 just makes fresh=false). The 4,000 ms timeout passed at live.mjs:315 compounds this: a 1-2 MB body that is under the cap but slow to arrive is aborted in App.tsx:70 and also lands in the same silent-retry path. Partially refuted: (1) the trigger is narrower than claimed. The real capture tests/fixtures/chicago-feed.json (Chicago, 28 Oct 2026) reports total:334 aircraft at roughly 60 NM (~560 B/aircraft minified = ~190 KB); crossing 2 MB needs ~3,700 aircraft inside the 250 NM circle, which is plausible only around the very densest corridors (NYC/Northeast, London/Benelux/Rhine-Main) at peak hours and cannot be verified without a live request, which this review was not allowed to make. (2) It is not 'permanently dead': the feed recovers as soon as traffic drops below the threshold or the user picks a smaller radius; the user must have deliberately chosen the 150/250 mi extreme. (3) '>11 GB/day' assumes uncompressed transfer; adsb.fi serves gzip and RN fetch decompresses transparently, so wire traffic is roughly an order of magnitude lower, though the wasted server work per 15 s poll stands. (4) The checkCoverage (live.mjs:306-311) part is not a problem: it runs only when the normal poll returned zero aircraft, i.e. in sparse areas where the 250 NM reply is small. Net: a real, narrow robustness gap (no 'oversize'/timeout handling, cap enforced after full download, wide radii combined with a 4 s timeout) affecting only users who select the widest radii in the busiest airspace at peak; fix suggestions (treat 'oversize' distinctly with back-off and radius step-down, check Content-Length/abort early, or cap searchNm lower) are appropriate. P3, not P2.

confirmed.title: Atlas Satellite re-fetches up to 48 imagery tiles from USGS/EOX on every redraw, including each Settings step and each map-radius step (several redraws per step)
confirmed.trigger: Layout atlas-satellite active. drawSatellite runs from drawMap, which runs on mount, setMap and refresh (atlas.mjs:350-353). app.mjs calls refreshLayout on every Settings value change (line 347: units, place names, alert radius, font…) and stepMap/cancelEdit call mapsChanged()+refreshLayout() back to back (lines 390, 405), followed by applyPlace's mapsChanged when the base and then the detail map arrive.
confirmed.impact: One radius step issues 3-5 drawSatellite passes = up to 240 loads against basemap.nationalmap.gov or tiles.maps.eox.at; stepping through all radii issues thousands. The images are dropped after drawing (`img.src=''`) so nothing is reused in-page; only the WebView's HTTP cache (if the servers' cache headers allow and the stick's cache holds 48 JPEGs) prevents real re-downloads. Failed tiles have no onerror handling, so a tile lost to a blip stays blank until the next redraw (and a 429 is answered by the next redraw's burst).
confirmed.evidence: atlas.mjs:158-164 `for(let x=x0;x<=x1;x++)for(let y=y0;y<=y1;y++){ const img=new Image(); img.onload=()=>{ ... g.drawImage(...);img.src=''; }; img.src=(us?USGS:EOX).replace(...); }`; atlas.mjs:167-168 `function drawMap(){ drawSatellite(); ...`; :351 `setMap(m){maps=m;drawMap();}` :353 `refresh(){drawMap();}`; app.mjs:390 and :405 `busy(()=>{mapsChanged();refreshLayout();});`
confirmed.fix: Keep the decoded satellite canvas (or the Image objects) keyed by {z, x0..x1, y0..y1} and skip drawSatellite when the key is unchanged; split refresh() so Settings changes that don't move the view don't touch the imagery; add onerror with a single delayed retry per tile and skip redraw bursts while one is in flight (satToken already exists).
reasons: UPHELD: The code path is real and the claim reproduces as described. web/layouts/atlas.mjs:141-165 drawSatellite() has no view/zoom key or cache: every call bumps satToken, repaints, computes the tile grid and issues up to 48 `new Image()` loads against USGS/EOX (the token only suppresses drawImage for superseded passes, not the request itself); each Image is dropped via img.src='' after drawing, so nothing in-page is reused. drawMap() calls drawSatellite() unconditionally (atlas.mjs:167), and drawMap runs from mount, setMap(m) and refresh() (atlas.mjs:351-353). Callers in web/app.mjs: refreshLayout() (line 218) calls mod.refresh() and is invoked on every non-map Settings adjustment (line 347 `busy(refreshLayout)`, e.g. units/place names/font), and for alert radius (line 346); stepMap (line 405) and cancelEdit (line 390) do `mapsChanged();refreshLayout();` back to back = 2 drawSatellite passes immediately, then applyPlace after 700 ms (line 407) calls mapsChanged when base and/or detail maps change (lines 178, 187 and ensureDetail 136/143), giving 3-5 passes per radius step. Zoom depends on radius (ppmOf -> zoom(), kit.mjs:222), so the tile set changes per step and the same URLs are re-requested on each of the redundant passes within a step. There is indeed no onerror handler on the tiles, so a failed tile stays blank until the next redraw. confirmed.title: Address search: the 25 s UI deadline is shorter than the geocoder chain's worst case, and 'Try again' starts a second chain while the first keeps running
confirmed.trigger: Slow network (each call near its timeout) during an explicit street-address Search in the US: Census (10 s, 12 s via bridge) + up to 4 sequential Open-Meteo time-zone lookups (6 s/8 s each) + Nominatim (10 s/12 s) + up to 4 more TZ lookups = up to ~88 s of sequential requests; runSearch races this against SEARCH_LIMIT_MS = 25,000.
confirmed.impact: On a slow link the user is shown 'The search is taking too long.' with a Try again button while the original chain continues issuing Census/Open-Meteo/Nominatim requests whose result will be discarded (seq mismatch). Each Try again press starts another full chain concurrently, so an impatient user generates 2-3 parallel Nominatim + Census + 8 TZ request chains for one address, contrary to Nominatim's one-request-per-search intent stated in the comment. No results are lost in the common case, but request volume to three third parties multiplies under exactly the conditions (congestion) where it should fall.
confirmed.evidence: place.mjs:111 `await getJson(CENSUS_URL(q),10000)`; :115-121 `for(const m of matches.slice(0,4)){ ... const p=await addZone({...}) }` with addZone :101 `getJson(TZ_URL(...),6000)`; :124 `await getJson(NOMINATIM_URL(q),10000)`; :127-133 second loop of up to 4 addZone; app.mjs:462 `const SEARCH_LIMIT_MS=25000;` :482 `const found=await Promise.race([work,new Promise(r=>setTimeout(()=>r('timeout'),SEARCH_LIMIT_MS))]);` :526 `case 'search-retry': ... return runSearch(true);`
confirmed.fix: Run the per-match time-zone lookups in parallel (Promise.all) or defer them until a match is chosen (one TZ lookup instead of up to 8), pass an AbortSignal/seq into searchAddress so a superseded or timed-out search stops issuing requests, and disable Try again while a chain for the same query is still in flight.
reasons: UPHELD: Code path confirmed. web/place.mjs:106-137 searchAddress awaits sequentially: Census getJson(…,10000) at :111, then up to 4 addZone calls (each getJson(TZ_URL,6000) at :101) inside `for(const m of matches.slice(0,4))` at :115-121, then Nominatim getJson(…,10000) at :124, then up to 4 more addZone at :127-133. web/live.mjs:21-31 shows the bridge path resolves on a page-side timer of timeoutMs+2000 (so 12 s / 8 s), and src/App.tsx:211-214 clamps native timeouts to 12 s, so worst case is ~12+32+12+32 = 88 s, matching the claim; even Census alone plus its 4 TZ lookups (12+32 = 44 s) exceeds SEARCH_LIMIT_MS=25000 (app.mjs:461). app.mjs:482 uses Promise.race with a plain setTimeout; nothing aborts or signals `work`, and searchAddress takes no AbortSignal/seq, so the abandoned chain keeps issuing Census/TZ/Nominatim requests whose result is dropped at :483 by the seq check. app.mjs:526 'search-retry' calls runSearch(true) unconditionally with no in-flight guard, so each press starts another parallel chain. Severity stays P3: each request is individually time-limited, a chain is bounded to 10 requests, it only occurs on explicit user action under slow-network conditions, and no results are lost or wrong; the impact is multiplied third-party request volume (contrary to the one-request-per-search comment at place.mjs:105 / app.mjs:458-459) and a misleading 'taking too long' message while work is still underway. Suggested fix stands: parallelize or defer TZ lookups, thread an abort/seq into searchAddress, and disable Try again while a chain for the same query is in flight.

UPHELD: Confirmed from the code; nothing elsewhere mitigates it. web/place.mjs:107-135 searchAddress is strictly sequential: Census getJson(...,10000) at :111, then `for(const m of matches.slice(0,4)) await addZone(...)` at :115-121 (addZone :101 getJson(TZ_URL,6000)), then Nominatim getJson(...,10000) at :124, then another up-to-4 sequential addZone loop at :127-133. No AbortSignal/seq is threaded in; web/live.mjs:21-31 getJson in bridge mode has no abort path at all (only its own timer, timeoutMs+2000), and src/App.tsx:211-214 clamps each request to <=12 s but has no in-flight dedup or per-host concurrency limit. So worst case is ~12+4*8+12+4*8 = 88 s of serial requests, and even the common slow case (Census near 10 s + 4 TZ near 6 s) exceeds SEARCH_LIMIT_MS=25000 at web/app.mjs:462. runSearch :482 races against the 25 s timer, :483 drops a late result via `seq!==searchSeq`, but the `work` promise keeps running and keeps issuing requests. :486 shows 'The search is taking too long.' with a Try again button; select() :526 `case 'search-retry'` and typeKey :453 `key==='search'` both call runSearch(true) unconditionally with no in-flight guard, so each press starts a fresh full chain concurrently with the still-running ones. Impact is bounded (extra Census/Open-Meteo/Nominatim requests and a misleading timeout message; no data loss, no crash), so P3 is the right severity. Suggested fix stands: parallelize or defer per-match TZ lookups, pass seq/AbortSignal into searchAddress and check it between steps, and ignore Search/Try again while a chain for the same query is in flight.

UPHELD: Verified against the code; the claim holds as stated and I could not find a mitigating mechanism.

Mechanics confirmed:
- web/place.mjs:111 Census getJson(...,10000); :115-121 sequential `for...await addZone` over up to 4 matches, addZone at :101 is getJson(TZ_URL,6000); :124 Nominatim getJson(...,10000); :127-133 another sequential loop of up to 4 addZone. Nothing in searchAddress takes a signal/seq, and getJson (web/live.mjs:21-31) over the bridge has no cancellation path at all: the web-side timer only resolves the promise after timeoutMs+2000; the native fetch keeps running until its own timeout (src/App.tsx:69-70,211-215). So the chain's effective worst case is 12 + 4x8 + 12 + 4x8 = 88 s, vs SEARCH_LIMIT_MS=25000 at app.mjs:462 and the Promise.race at :482.
- app.mjs:483 discards a late result by seq mismatch only; the `work` promise and its remaining requests are not stopped. :526 'search-retry' calls runSearch(true) unconditionally, which bumps searchSeq and starts a fresh searchAddress while the previous one is still issuing Census/Open-Meteo/Nominatim requests. No in-flight guard exists (grep for searchSeq/runSearch shows none).

Realism check (the skeptic lens): the pure-failure path is fine, since Census fail (12 s) + Nominatim fail (12 s) = 24 s < 25 s, so the limit was evidently tuned for that. But the mixed path is realistic, not exotic: Census succeeding normally (~2 s) with 3-4 candidate matches while Open-Meteo is slow/unreachable costs 2 + 3x8 = 26 s or 2 + 4x8 = 34 s, which trips the 25 s limit even though usable results (addZone still returns a place when TZ fails) arrive seconds later. In that state every Try again reproduces the same timeout and adds another concurrent 4-5 request chain, exactly the request multiplication under congestion that the claim describes, and contrary to the "one request per search" comment at app.mjs:459-460 / place.mjs:106.

Severity: for a TV user the effect is a confusing "taking too long" + retry loop during a one-time setup flow, plus 2-3x redundant third-party traffic; no data corruption, no crash, results are recoverable on a healthier link. P3 is the right level. Suggested fix (parallel or deferred TZ lookups, a seq/AbortSignal check between steps in searchAddress, disable Try again while a chain is in flight) is proportionate and correct.

confirmed.title: When saveDetail fails on localStorage quota the street map is silently rebuilt (28-56 tiles + tilejson) on every launch and every switch to a detail layout
confirmed.trigger: localStorage near its quota (known item 12 measured ~4.3 MB; a 15 mi detail map alone is ~2.3 MB per the code comment, Chicago). setItem throws, saveDetail removes the key and returns false; app.mjs:142 ignores the return value.
confirmed.impact: savedDetail then finds nothing, so ensureDetail runs buildDetail again on every app launch and every layout switch into Atlas/Glass/Blueprint (useLayout -> ensureDetail), each time fetching 1 tilejson + 28-56 vector tiles (measured per radius) from OpenFreeMap and spending seconds decoding on the stick. The user sees 'Drawing the street map…' at every start and never learns why. With the orphan-build issue above, a quick layout flip during the build doubles it.
confirmed.evidence: mapgen.mjs:362-366 `export function saveDetail(m){ const key=...; try{localStorage.setItem(key,JSON.stringify(m));return true;} catch{try{localStorage.removeItem(key);}catch{} return false;} }`; app.mjs:142 `saveDetail(built);` (return value unused); app.mjs:119 `if(mod.map==='detail')ensureDetail();`
confirmed.fix: When saveDetail returns false, free space first (drop the other detail slot and the oldest base maps via RECENT_KEY, then retry setItem) and, if it still fails, keep the built map in memory for the session (maps.detail) and record a 'detail-unsaveable' flag with a timestamp so the rebuild is attempted at most once per day rather than per launch/switch; show a one-line note in Settings.
reasons: UPHELD: The code path is real and reproduces as described. web/mapgen.mjs:362-366 saveDetail: on setItem throw it removes the key and returns false. web/app.mjs:142 calls saveDetail(built) and discards the result. Line 113 sets maps.detail=null whenever the active layout is not a detail layout (Atlas, Glass, Blueprint, Sectional per layouts/*.mjs map:'detail'), and line 119 calls ensureDetail() on every switch into one; ensureDetail (132-136) consults only savedDetail(), which returns null once the save failed, so buildDetail runs again (tilejson + z12/z14 tiles via the bridge, decode on the stick) with 'Drawing the street map…' shown and no indication of the cause. At launch (app.mjs:671 useLayout(settings.layout)) maps.detail is empty, so the same rebuild happens every start. Within one session the built map is kept in memory (line 143) until the user leaves a detail layout, which only narrows the claim slightly ('every switch into a detail layout from a non-detail one'). Trigger plausibility is backed by the repo's own measurement (qa/PRESHIP-REPORT.md P2-6: storage peaks at ~4.3 MB with 2 detail maps and 3 base maps; mapgen.mjs:239-240 notes ~2.3 MB for a 15 mi Chicago street map), and nothing in saveDetail or saveMap frees other map slots before retrying. Not a functional failure (the map still renders each time), so P3 for wasted network/CPU and a confusing recurring progress note is the right severity.

UPHELD: The mechanics check out and nothing elsewhere compensates. web/mapgen.mjs:362-366: saveDetail swallows the setItem failure, removes the key and returns false; the comment at :352 ("Too big for the quota: not saved") confirms this is the only handling. web/app.mjs:142 discards the return value; there is no eviction or retry anywhere (saveMap at mapgen.mjs:219-224 trims base maps only when a base map is saved, never on a detail-save failure; live.mjs store.set likewise silently swallows quota errors). Consequence path verified: app.mjs:113 sets maps.detail=null whenever a non-detail layout is mounted, and app.mjs:119/134-136 run ensureDetail -> savedDetail -> null -> buildDetail (1 tilejson + full tile fetch via the bridge, no native cache found in src/App.tsx) on every detail-layout mount and every launch. The only mitigation is that app.mjs:143 keeps the built map in memory while the user stays on a detail layout, so within one session it is rebuilt once per switch into Atlas/Glass/Blueprint, not continuously. Trigger plausibility: two detail slots (street ~2.3 MB at 15 mi per the comment at :239-240, plus a wide slot) and up to three base maps all share one origin quota, and JSON strings are often counted as UTF-16 by WebView quota accounting, so hitting the limit on a 5-10 MB quota is realistic for large-metro homes; the user gets 'Drawing the street map…' on every start with no explanation. No test covers the failure path. Severity stays P3: graceful degradation (the map still appears), but repeated multi-tile fetches from OpenFreeMap on every launch is real wasted bandwidth and startup latency. Suggested fix as claimed: on false, evict the other detail slot / oldest base maps and retry, else record a short-lived 'unsaveable' marker to rate-limit rebuilds.

rejected.title: Logbook `typesAll` keeps one key per distinct feed `aircraft_type` forever, with no length or count cap: three polls poison localStorage permanently
reasons: REFUTED: The claimed trigger does not reproduce on the real code path. liveSource (web/model.mjs:208) builds `planes` from `airspace()` in web/core.mjs, not from live.mjs `selection()`. core.mjs:49 defines `clean = v => typeof v==='string' ? v.trim().slice(0,24) : ''` and core.mjs:101 applies it as `aircraft_type:clean(a.t)`, so every `typesAll` key is at most 24 characters. Re-running the claim's scenario through the actual path (300 planes/poll, 6 KB `t` values, via airspace -> updateLog) gives: poll 1 = 1 typesAll key, maxKeyLen 24, log JSON 17.5 KB; poll 3 = 52 KB (growth is the hex-keyed `planes` map, itself capped at 4000 entries at model.mjs:99). The claim's 3.6 MB/7.2 MB/10.8 MB figures are only obtainable by calling updateLog with records that bypassed core's `clean()`, which the app never does. live.mjs `selection()` (line 89, no clean) only feeds `mergeHistory` -> HISTORY_KEY, which is capped at 20 rows (live.mjs:106), and the whole feed response is capped at 2 MB by App.tsx MAX_BYTES (line 34), so that cannot grow without bound either. The "nothing in the app can clear it" statement is also wrong: app.mjs:171 calls resetLog() whenever the home place is changed (fresh=true). Residual hardening note (not the P2 claimed): because typesAll has no key-count cap and planes-map FIFO lets hexes be recycled, a hostile/compromised adsb.fi response could still add up to ~300 distinct 24-char keys per poll (~10 KB/poll), growing across days; a cap on typesAll key count (e.g. drop lowest counts above 2,000) would close that, but it requires a malicious upstream over HTTPS, not three ordinary polls, and the per-tick stringify stays in the tens-of-KB range for real feeds.

REFUTED: The central premise ("300 planes x 6 KB type strings per poll", 3.6 MB per poll) is false on the real code path. `liveSource` (web/model.mjs:208) builds `planes` from `airspace()` in web/core.mjs, and core.mjs:101 sets `aircraft_type:clean(a.t)` where `clean = v => typeof v==='string' ? v.trim().slice(0,24) : ''` (core.mjs:49). `enrich()` (model.mjs:161-179) spreads `...a` and does not re-read `raw.t`, so every key written to `log.typesAll` at model.mjs:98 is at most 24 characters. Verified with a node snippet feeding 300 entries with 6,000-char `t` values through `airspace()`: all 300 records came out with `aircraft_type.length === 24`. The uncleaned `selection()` path at live.mjs:88 that the claim cites only feeds `mergeHistory` (live.mjs:98-105), which is capped at 20 rows and never touches `typesAll`. The claim's measured 3.6/7.2/10.8 MB figures can only be obtained by calling `updateLog` directly with records that bypassed `airspace()`, which the app never does. `store.set` (live.mjs:63) also wraps `setItem` in try/catch, so a quota error degrades to memory-only rather than throwing. What remains is a much smaller hardening gap: `typesAll` has no key-count cap (unlike `planes` at 4000 and `seen` at 3000), so a fully hostile/compromised adsb.fi response emitting 300 fresh 6-hex `hex` values with 300 distinct <=24-char `t` values every 5 s could add roughly 10 KB per poll, i.e. on the order of 40+ minutes of continuous malicious feed to approach a 5 MB quota; with the genuine feed the key space is the few hundred ICAO type designators and the structure stays a few KB forever. That residual is a P3 hardening item (cap `typesAll` key count / restrict to `/^[A-Z0-9]{2,4}$/`), not the P2 "three polls poison localStorage permanently" defect claimed.

UPHELD: Mechanics confirmed: web/live.mjs:89 passes feed `t` through untyped and uncapped (clean()'s 24-char cap is display-only), web/model.mjs:98 tallies log.typesAll[a.aircraft_type] for every new hex before the 15 NM filter, model.mjs:84 carries typesAll across every day rollover with no prune, and model.mjs:218 stringifies+setItems the whole log every fresh tick. A pure-function probe (no I/O) reproduced the numbers: 300 planes x 6 KB distinct `t` per poll -> 3.45/6.89/10.34 MB log JSON after polls 1-3, 900 keys and 5.16 MB still present two simulated days later. However, the stated impact and severity are overstated for a TV user: (1) "nothing can clear it" is false, web/app.mjs:216 and :689 call applyPlace(place,{fresh:true}) which calls resetLog(); changing home in Settings (or clearing app data) wipes the log; (2) src/App.tsx:34 caps every bridged response at 2 MB, so a single poll cannot carry more than that; (3) store.set (live.mjs:63) swallows QuotaExceeded and keeps the value in memory, so the app keeps running; the persisted damage is capped at the localStorage quota and manifests as a multi-MB log parsed at launch/re-stringified per tick plus map caches failing to persist (tiles re-fetched each launch); (4) the trust model: `t` is adsb.fi's own database field (not broadcast by aircraft), delivered from the single hard-coded allow-listed HTTPS origin, so the attack requires adsb.fi itself or a TLS MITM to be hostile, and such an upstream can already degrade the app per-session by other means (2 MB garbage, huge `r`/`flight` strings on 300 planes). Benign data (2-4 char ICAO designators, a few thousand possible values) keeps typesAll in the tens of KB forever. Net: a real but low-likelihood hardening gap with bounded, user-reversible impact; cheap fix is to sanitise aircraft_type in selection() (string, trim, cap length, e.g. /^[A-Z0-9]{2,4}$/i for the tally) and cap typesAll key count.
